aws_access_analyzer_analyzer: `aws_access_analyzer_analyzer` creates an IAM Access Analyzer, a real analyzer that continuously scans resource policies (S3 buckets, IAM roles, KMS keys, and similar) and reports which grant access to anything outside the account or organization it's scoped to. Analyzers come in a few real, distinct modes, external access, unused access, and internal access, and the same resource also drives policy validation and policy generation from real CloudTrail activity.
aws_account_access_application: `aws_account_access_application` is part of IAM Identity Center's account access manager, which manages applications and entitlements that grant Identity Center principals access to IAM roles across accounts. An application in this context represents one such cross-account access grant, connecting a principal to a real IAM role in a target account without a standalone permission set.
aws_account_access_entitlement: `aws_account_access_entitlement` is the entitlement half of IAM Identity Center's account access manager, the specific permission grant attached to an `aws_account_access_application`. It is what actually authorizes a principal to assume the application's target role, real, revocable access rather than an implicit side effect of the application existing.
aws_acmpca_certificate: `aws_acmpca_certificate` is a certificate issued by an `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority`. AWS Private CA issues it against the CA's own signing key and policy, the certificate itself carries no independent configuration beyond what its issuing CA allows.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority: `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority` creates a private certificate authority, root or subordinate, that issues and revokes X.509 certificates for internal PKI. It's regionally scoped, integrates with services like ACM and IoT Core for automated certificate issuance, and its private key never leaves AWS's managed HSM boundary.
aws_agent_registry_registry: `aws_agent_registry_registry` creates a private, governed catalog for discovering agents, tools, skills, and MCP servers inside Bedrock AgentCore. It's the container that org-wide publishing and discovery of these resources happens through, rather than each team maintaining its own ad hoc list.
aws_agent_registry_registry_record: `aws_agent_registry_registry_record` represents the metadata for one individual resource, an agent, a tool, an MCP server, published into an `aws_agent_registry_registry`. It's the actual catalog entry a consumer discovers and resolves, not the underlying resource itself.
aws_aiops_investigation_group: `aws_aiops_investigation_group` is a one-time setup resource for CloudWatch investigations, the generative AI-assisted incident response capability that correlates signals across an account during an active issue. One investigation group per region holds the central settings, encryption and retention among them, that every investigation in that region inherits.
aws_amazon_mq_broker: `aws_amazon_mq_broker` creates the actual message broker environment, ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ, that Amazon MQ runs. It's the basic building block of the service, everything else, configuration, users, network placement, attaches to a broker rather than existing independently.
aws_amazon_mq_configuration: `aws_amazon_mq_configuration` defines the engine-specific settings (XML for ActiveMQ, a config file for RabbitMQ) that an `aws_amazon_mq_broker` runs with, kept as a separate, versioned resource so the same configuration can be validated and reused across brokers instead of being edited in place on each one.
aws_amazon_mq_configuration_association: `aws_amazon_mq_configuration_association` is the real link between an `aws_amazon_mq_configuration` and the `aws_amazon_mq_broker` it applies to. A configuration on its own changes nothing, this association is what actually applies a given configuration revision to a running broker.
aws_amplify_app: `aws_amplify_app` creates the top-level Amplify Hosting application, the Git-connected project that Amplify's managed CI/CD pipeline builds and deploys from. Branches, domains, and build settings all attach to this app rather than standing alone.
aws_amplify_branch: `aws_amplify_branch` connects one Git branch of an `aws_amplify_app` to its own real, independently deployed environment, so pushing to `main` and pushing to a feature branch produce two separate, live URLs rather than one shared deployment.
aws_amplify_domain: `aws_amplify_domain` attaches a custom domain to an `aws_amplify_app` and maps its subdomains to specific branches, real DNS and SSL provisioning included, rather than leaving the app reachable only at its default `amplifyapp.com` URL.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component: `aws_amplify_uibuilder_component` is a UI component generated by Amplify Studio, commonly converted automatically from a Figma design into real, editable React component code rather than hand-written from scratch.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form: `aws_amplify_uibuilder_form` is Amplify Studio's form-building counterpart to `aws_amplify_uibuilder_component`, a generated, data-bound form definition rather than a hand-assembled one, wired to an app's real data model.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme: `aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme` defines the shared visual styling, colors, typography, spacing, that Amplify Studio applies consistently across an app's generated components and forms, so design changes happen in one place rather than per component.
aws_api_gateway_account: `aws_api_gateway_account` configures account-wide REST API Gateway settings, most notably the IAM role API Gateway assumes to push execution logs to CloudWatch, applying once per account rather than per `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`.
aws_api_gateway_api_key: `aws_api_gateway_api_key` issues a key that identifies a caller against an `aws_api_gateway_usage_plan`, the real mechanism REST APIs use to meter and throttle usage per consumer rather than per IAM identity.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer: `aws_api_gateway_authorizer` attaches a Lambda-, Cognito-, or IAM-based access-control check to an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`, run before a request reaches its backend integration, so authorization logic lives outside the backend rather than duplicated inside it.
aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping: `aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping` maps a path segment on an `aws_api_gateway_domain_name` to a specific REST API and stage, the real mechanism that lets one custom domain front several different APIs at different base paths.
aws_api_gateway_client_certificate: `aws_api_gateway_client_certificate` generates a certificate an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api` presents to its own backend, so the backend can verify requests genuinely came through API Gateway rather than directly from the internet.
aws_api_gateway_deployment: `aws_api_gateway_deployment` is a real, immutable snapshot of an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`'s resources and methods at a point in time. A REST API's configuration only takes effect once deployed, and a deployment only becomes reachable once an `aws_api_gateway_stage` points to it.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part: `aws_api_gateway_documentation_part` is one documented fragment, a description of a specific method, resource, or parameter, that rolls up into an `aws_api_gateway_documentation_version` for an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_version: `aws_api_gateway_documentation_version` snapshots an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`'s documentation parts at a point in time, kept versioned separately from the API's own deployments so docs and API behavior can each move independently.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name: `aws_api_gateway_domain_name` registers a custom domain for REST APIs (API Gateway v1), provisioning the TLS certificate and edge or regional endpoint that requests to that domain terminate at, before `aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping` routes them to a specific API.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2: `aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2` is the newer resource type for the same custom-domain concept as `aws_api_gateway_domain_name`, supporting multi-level base path mappings that the original resource type doesn't.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response: `aws_api_gateway_gateway_response` customizes the response API Gateway itself returns for a given error, a 4XX or 5XX that never reached the backend, on an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`, overriding the default generic error body and headers.
aws_api_gateway_method: `aws_api_gateway_method` defines one HTTP method (GET, POST, and similar) on an `aws_api_gateway_resource`, together with its own authorization, request validation, and backend integration, the real unit a REST API caller actually invokes.
aws_api_gateway_model: `aws_api_gateway_model` is a JSON Schema definition attached to an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api`, used by request validators and documentation to describe the real shape of a request or response body rather than leaving it untyped.
aws_api_gateway_request_validator: `aws_api_gateway_request_validator` attaches to an `aws_api_gateway_method` and rejects malformed requests, missing required parameters or a body that doesn't match its `aws_api_gateway_model`, before they ever reach the backend integration.
aws_api_gateway_resource: `aws_api_gateway_resource` defines one path segment in a REST API's URL tree, nested under an `aws_api_gateway_rest_api` (or under another resource), with one or more `aws_api_gateway_method`s attached to actually handle requests at that path.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api: `aws_api_gateway_rest_api` creates the REST API itself, the container for an API Gateway v1 (REST API) deployment. Resources, methods, and deployments all nest inside it, and it's the unit that gets versioned and deployed to a stage as a whole.
aws_api_gateway_stage: `aws_api_gateway_stage` is a named, addressable environment (`prod`, `dev`, and similar) that points at a specific `aws_api_gateway_deployment`. Callers hit a stage's own URL, and promoting a new version means moving the stage to point at a new deployment, not editing the API in place.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan: `aws_api_gateway_usage_plan` defines throttling and quota limits for one or more REST APIs and stages, and the `aws_api_gateway_api_key`s associated with it are what identify which caller a given request's usage counts against.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan_key: `aws_api_gateway_usage_plan_key` is the actual association between an `aws_api_gateway_api_key` and an `aws_api_gateway_usage_plan`. An API key on its own is subject to no limits, this association is what puts it under a specific plan's throttling and quota.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api: `aws_api_gateway_v2_api` creates an HTTP API or WebSocket API, API Gateway v2's lighter-weight, lower-latency alternative to a v1 REST API, purpose-built for proxying to Lambda or an HTTP backend rather than the full feature set REST APIs offer.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o: `aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_overrides` lets specific settings on an API Gateway-managed `aws_api_gateway_v2_stage` be overridden without disconnecting the stage from Gateway's own automatic management of it.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_mapping: `aws_api_gateway_v2_api_mapping` maps an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api` and stage onto a path under an `aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name`, the v2 equivalent of a v1 base path mapping.
aws_api_gateway_v2_authorizer: `aws_api_gateway_v2_authorizer` attaches a Lambda-, JWT-, or IAM-based access check to an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api`, evaluated before a request reaches its integration, the v2 counterpart to a v1 REST API authorizer.
aws_api_gateway_v2_deployment: `aws_api_gateway_v2_deployment` is a snapshot of an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api`'s routes and integrations at a point in time, the v2 counterpart to a v1 REST API deployment, made reachable once an `aws_api_gateway_v2_stage` points to it.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name: `aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name` registers a custom domain for HTTP or WebSocket APIs, provisioning the TLS certificate and endpoint that requests terminate at before an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api_mapping` routes them to a specific API and stage.
aws_api_gateway_v2_integration: `aws_api_gateway_v2_integration` connects an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api`'s routes to a real backend, Lambda, an HTTP endpoint, or another AWS service, the actual mechanism that determines what happens once a request matches a route.
aws_api_gateway_v2_integration_response: `aws_api_gateway_v2_integration_response` transforms the response an `aws_api_gateway_v2_integration` returns before it goes back to the caller, used on WebSocket APIs where response mapping isn't handled automatically the way it is for HTTP APIs.
aws_api_gateway_v2_model: `aws_api_gateway_v2_model` is a JSON Schema definition attached to an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api`, the v2 counterpart to a v1 REST API model, describing the expected shape of a request or response body.
aws_api_gateway_v2_route_response: `aws_api_gateway_v2_route_response` defines the response a WebSocket API route sends back after its `aws_api_gateway_v2_integration_response` runs, part of the two-way message flow WebSocket APIs support that HTTP APIs don't need.
aws_api_gateway_v2_routing_rule: `aws_api_gateway_v2_routing_rule` defines additional request-matching logic for an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api`'s routes beyond the basic method-and-path match, used to route the same path differently based on request content.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage: `aws_api_gateway_v2_stage` is a named, addressable environment for an HTTP or WebSocket API that points at a specific `aws_api_gateway_v2_deployment`, the v2 counterpart to a v1 REST API stage.
aws_api_gateway_v2_vpc_link: `aws_api_gateway_v2_vpc_link` lets an `aws_api_gateway_v2_api` integration reach a private resource inside a VPC (an internal load balancer, for instance) without that resource being exposed to the public internet, the v2 counterpart to a v1 REST API VPC link.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link: `aws_api_gateway_vpc_link` lets a REST API's integration reach a private resource inside a VPC, typically a Network Load Balancer in front of an internal service, without that resource ever being exposed publicly.
aws_app_config_application: `aws_app_config_application` is the top-level container in AWS AppConfig, the logical grouping that an `aws_app_config_environment` and `aws_app_config_configuration_profile` both attach to. AppConfig itself lets you change application behavior, feature flags, allow lists, throttling limits, in production without redeploying code.
aws_app_config_configuration_profile: `aws_app_config_configuration_profile` defines how AppConfig locates and manages one piece of configuration data, either a feature-flag profile or a free-form configuration sourced from S3, SSM Parameter Store, Secrets Manager, or AppConfig's own hosted store, with optional validators that block a bad deployment before it ships.
aws_app_config_deployment: `aws_app_config_deployment` starts the actual rollout of a specific configuration version to an `aws_app_config_environment`, following a chosen `aws_app_config_deployment_strategy` and validated against any validators the `aws_app_config_configuration_profile` defines, with automatic CloudWatch-alarm-triggered rollback if something breaks mid-rollout.
aws_app_config_deployment_strategy: `aws_app_config_deployment_strategy` defines how gradually a configuration change rolls out, the percentage growth rate and bake time between steps, so a change reaches a small slice of an environment first and only expands once it's proven safe.
aws_app_config_environment: `aws_app_config_environment` is a logical deployment target inside an `aws_app_config_application`, Beta or Production for the whole app, or Web, Mobile, and Backend for its subcomponents, with its own CloudWatch alarms that AppConfig monitors during a deployment and rolls back on if one trips.
aws_app_config_experiment_definition: `aws_app_config_experiment_definition` runs a real A/B test or gradual rollout on production traffic, built directly on top of AppConfig's own feature-flag configuration profiles rather than a separate experimentation stack, splitting traffic between variants and tracking operational metrics through CloudWatch as exposure increases.
aws_app_config_extension: `aws_app_config_extension` defines custom or AWS-authored behavior, notify SNS or EventBridge, run a Lambda check, that AppConfig invokes at specific lifecycle points (before a hosted configuration is created, or when a deployment starts, completes, or rolls back).
aws_app_config_extension_association: `aws_app_config_extension_association` attaches an `aws_app_config_extension` to a specific AppConfig resource, an application or a configuration profile, and is what actually invokes the extension at its defined lifecycle points. An extension defined but never associated never runs.
aws_app_flow_connector_profile: `aws_app_flow_connector_profile` stores the authenticated connection details, credentials and endpoint, for one SaaS source or destination (Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, and similar), that an `aws_app_flow_flow` then draws on to move data without re-authenticating per flow.
aws_app_flow_flow: `aws_app_flow_flow` defines one real data transfer between a source and destination, on demand or on a schedule, using the connections an `aws_app_flow_connector_profile` establishes. It's the actual unit of work Amazon AppFlow runs, field mappings, transformations, and trigger included.
aws_app_integrations_application: `aws_app_integrations_application` configures a reusable connection to an external application inside Amazon AppIntegrations, most commonly consumed by Amazon Connect's own third-party integrations, the general application-level counterpart to a specific `aws_app_integrations_data_integration` or `aws_app_integrations_event_integration`.
aws_app_integrations_data_integration: `aws_app_integrations_data_integration` configures a bulk or bidirectional data connection to an external application, defining what data AppIntegrations pulls in and how it's kept current, distinct from the real-time streaming an `aws_app_integrations_event_integration` handles.
aws_app_integrations_event_integration: `aws_app_integrations_event_integration` streams events from a partner application into an EventBridge event bus, with its own filters and event sources, so downstream AWS services can react to changes in an external system in near real time rather than polling for them.
aws_app_mesh_gateway_route: `aws_app_mesh_gateway_route` matches incoming traffic at an `aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway` and directs it to a virtual service inside the mesh, the ingress counterpart to the routes an `aws_app_mesh_virtual_router` uses for traffic already inside the mesh.
aws_app_mesh_mesh: `aws_app_mesh_mesh` creates the service mesh itself, the logical boundary for all network traffic between the services registered inside it. Every other App Mesh resource, virtual nodes, routers, services, gateways, belongs to exactly one mesh.
aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway: `aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway` is the entry point for traffic coming into an `aws_app_mesh_mesh` from outside it, running the same Envoy proxy technology as a virtual node but for ingress rather than for a specific service.
aws_app_mesh_virtual_node: `aws_app_mesh_virtual_node` is a logical pointer to one real, discoverable service (an ECS service, a Kubernetes deployment) inside an `aws_app_mesh_mesh`. The proxy deployed alongside that real service reads its virtual node's configuration to decide how to route outbound traffic.
aws_app_mesh_virtual_router: `aws_app_mesh_virtual_router` handles traffic for one or more `aws_app_mesh_virtual_service`s, with routes that distribute traffic across `aws_app_mesh_virtual_node`s by weighted percentage, HTTP header, path, or gRPC method, the mechanism behind canary and blue/green traffic shifts without touching application code.
aws_app_mesh_virtual_service: `aws_app_mesh_virtual_service` is an abstraction of a real service, backed either directly by an `aws_app_mesh_virtual_node` or indirectly through an `aws_app_mesh_virtual_router`, named to match the real service's own discoverable name so other services can keep addressing it exactly as they did before App Mesh was introduced.
aws_app_runner_auto_scaling_configuratio: `aws_app_runner_auto_scaling_configuration` sets the minimum and maximum provisioned instance count and per-instance concurrency an `aws_app_runner_service` scales within, letting a service scale down to its floor when traffic is low rather than running fixed capacity.
aws_app_runner_observability_configurati: `aws_app_runner_observability_configuration` enables AWS X-Ray tracing for an `aws_app_runner_service`, kept as its own resource so the same tracing configuration can be reused across multiple services rather than redefined on each one.
aws_app_runner_service: `aws_app_runner_service` deploys source code or a container image directly to a running, scalable, load-balanced web service, without the caller provisioning or choosing underlying compute, App Runner builds and operates it end to end.
aws_app_runner_vpc_connector: `aws_app_runner_vpc_connector` gives an `aws_app_runner_service` outbound access into a VPC, specifying the subnets and security groups it uses, so the service can reach a private database or internal API that isn't exposed to the public internet.
aws_app_runner_vpc_ingress_connection: `aws_app_runner_vpc_ingress_connection` restricts an `aws_app_runner_service` to only be reachable from inside a VPC, connecting the service to a VPC interface endpoint so it accepts no traffic from the public internet at all. A service can have at most one of these.
aws_app_stream_app_block: `aws_app_stream_app_block` packages the application files and setup script needed to stream one application, built by an `aws_app_stream_app_block_builder` and uploaded to S3, the app-block model that lets an application be added to a stack without baking it into a full image.
aws_app_stream_app_block_builder: `aws_app_stream_app_block_builder` is the virtual machine used to create an `aws_app_stream_app_block`, packaging installed application content and uploading it to S3 to complete the app block, the app-block equivalent of what an `aws_app_stream_image_builder` does for full images.
aws_app_stream_application: `aws_app_stream_application` contains the information needed to actually launch one application to a streaming user, referencing the `aws_app_stream_app_block` or image that holds its real files.
aws_app_stream_application_entitlement_a: `aws_app_stream_application_entitlement_association` links a specific `aws_app_stream_application` to an `aws_app_stream_entitlement`, the actual grant that makes that one application, rather than every application in the stack, subject to that entitlement's SAML-based access rule.
aws_app_stream_application_fleet_associa: `aws_app_stream_application_fleet_association` links an `aws_app_stream_application` to the `aws_app_stream_fleet` it's actually streamed from, real for the app-block model where an application isn't already baked into a fleet's own image.
aws_app_stream_directory_config: `aws_app_stream_directory_config` stores the details AppStream needs to join image builders and fleet instances to an Active Directory domain, in a specific organizational unit, so streamed sessions can authenticate against a real corporate directory.
aws_app_stream_entitlement: `aws_app_stream_entitlement` controls access to specific applications in an AppStream stack based on SAML assertions from the identity provider, letting access to individual applications, not just to a stack as a whole, be driven by real group membership or attributes asserted at sign-in.
aws_app_stream_fleet: `aws_app_stream_fleet` provisions the streaming instances, EC2 instances made available one-per-user for the duration of a session, that run the applications and desktops an `aws_app_stream_stack` streams. The instance is terminated automatically once the session ends.
aws_app_stream_image_builder: `aws_app_stream_image_builder` is a virtual machine used to install, configure, and test applications before capturing them into an immutable image. Once an image is created it can't be edited in place, changing it means building a new image from a fresh image builder.
aws_app_stream_stack: `aws_app_stream_stack` bundles an `aws_app_stream_fleet`, user access policies, and storage configuration into the unit that actually streams applications to users. Users are entitled to stacks, not directly to fleets.
aws_app_stream_stack_fleet_association: `aws_app_stream_stack_fleet_association` links an `aws_app_stream_stack` to the `aws_app_stream_fleet` that actually runs its streaming instances. A stack with no fleet association has user access policies and storage configured but nothing to stream from.
aws_app_sync_api: `aws_app_sync_api` creates a GraphQL API in AWS AppSync, a managed, serverless endpoint that resolves queries against one or more real backend data sources, with built-in subscriptions for pushing real-time updates to connected clients.
aws_app_sync_api_cache: `aws_app_sync_api_cache` enables server-side caching for an `aws_app_sync_api`, holding resolver results in a managed, in-memory cache so repeated queries return with lower latency instead of re-invoking their data sources every time.
aws_app_sync_api_key: `aws_app_sync_api_key` issues a key-based credential for authorizing requests against an `aws_app_sync_api`, one of several supported authorization modes alongside IAM, Cognito, OpenID Connect, and Lambda authorizers.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace: `aws_app_sync_channel_namespace` defines a namespace for AWS AppSync Events, the WebSocket-powered real-time PubSub API AppSync supports separately from GraphQL subscriptions, scoping which channels a client can publish to and subscribe against.
aws_app_sync_data_source: `aws_app_sync_data_source` connects an `aws_app_sync_api` to a real backend, a DynamoDB table, a Lambda function, an HTTP endpoint, or another source, that an `aws_app_sync_resolver` then reads from or writes to when a matching query or mutation runs.
aws_app_sync_domain_name: `aws_app_sync_domain_name` registers a custom domain for an `aws_app_sync_api`, so a GraphQL endpoint is reachable at an organization's own domain rather than only at its default AppSync-issued URL.
aws_app_sync_domain_name_api_association: `aws_app_sync_domain_name_api_association` is the actual link between an `aws_app_sync_domain_name` and the `aws_app_sync_api` it should route to. A registered domain with no association routes nowhere.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi: `aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi` is the CloudFormation resource type for the same underlying concept as `aws_app_sync_api`, an AppSync GraphQL API, present as a distinct, older resource type in the CFN registry rather than a functionally different resource.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema: `aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema` is the GraphQL schema document attached to an `aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi`, the real type definitions AppSync validates queries and mutations against and routes to resolvers.
aws_app_sync_resolver: `aws_app_sync_resolver` maps one GraphQL field to a real operation against an `aws_app_sync_data_source`, written in JavaScript/TypeScript or Velocity Template Language, the actual logic that turns a GraphQL query into a request against a real backend and shapes its response back into the schema.
aws_app_sync_source_api_association: `aws_app_sync_source_api_association` links a source `aws_app_sync_api` into a merged API, AppSync's federation feature for combining multiple independently-owned GraphQL APIs into one endpoint that a client queries as if it were a single schema.
aws_app_test_test_case: `aws_app_test_test_case` defines the smallest real unit of a mainframe modernization test in AWS Mainframe Modernization Application Testing, typically one independent piece of business logic that modifies data, captured against the real mainframe and later replayed and compared against a modernized target.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta: `aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target` registers a scalable resource, a DynamoDB table, an ECS service, a Lambda function's provisioned concurrency, and many others, so Application Auto Scaling can manage its capacity within a defined minimum and maximum, the general-purpose scaling engine AWS provides for services outside EC2 Auto Scaling's own reach.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scaling_pol: `aws_application_auto_scaling_scaling_policy` defines how an `aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target` actually scales, target tracking against a CloudWatch metric, step scaling, scheduled scaling, or predictive scaling, the real logic a registered target has none of until a policy is attached.
aws_application_insights_application: `aws_application_insights_application` registers an application with CloudWatch Application Insights, which scans its component stack (databases, web and application servers, load balancers, queues) to recommend and set up key metrics, logs, and alarms, then correlates anomalies and errors into automated dashboards pointing at a likely root cause.
aws_application_signals_grouping_configu: `aws_application_signals_grouping_configuration` defines custom attributes, telemetry, AWS tags, or predefined mappings, that determine how CloudWatch Application Signals groups services in its console and APIs, overriding Application Signals's own default grouping by service dependency graph.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob: `aws_application_signals_service_level_objective` sets a target level of reliability or availability for a specific service in CloudWatch Application Signals, tracked against a service level indicator, typically latency or availability, so a team has a concrete, ongoing number for whether a service is meeting its own reliability bar.
aws_aps_anomaly_detector: `aws_aps_anomaly_detector` runs machine learning, specifically the Random Cut Forest algorithm, against a metric in an `aws_aps_workspace` to learn its normal pattern and flag deviations, producing new anomaly and confidence-score time series that can drive alerting rules or be visualized alongside the original metric.
aws_aps_rule_groups_namespace: `aws_aps_rule_groups_namespace` holds a set of Prometheus alerting and recording rules inside an `aws_aps_workspace`, the same PromQL-based rule mechanism open-source Prometheus uses, managed without the caller having to run and scale their own Alertmanager.
aws_aps_scraper: `aws_aps_scraper` is a fully managed collector that scrapes Prometheus metrics from an Amazon EKS cluster and writes them into an `aws_aps_workspace`, removing the need to run and scale a self-managed Prometheus server just to collect metrics.
aws_aps_workspace: `aws_aps_workspace` creates a Prometheus-compatible workspace, the top-level container Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus ingests, stores, and serves metrics from, replicated across three Availability Zones and retained for 150 days by default.
aws_arcregion_switch_plan: `aws_arcregion_switch_plan` defines a Region switch plan in Amazon Application Recovery Controller, the workflows, steps, and execution blocks that orchestrate moving a multi-Region application's traffic and data from one AWS Region to another in a coordinated, observable, automated way rather than as a manual runbook.
aws_arczonal_shift_autoshift_observer_no: `aws_arczonal_shift_autoshift_observer_notification_status` turns on autoshift observer notifications, EventBridge events for every autoshift ARC starts account-wide, even for resources that never had `aws_arczonal_shift_zonal_autoshift_configuration` enabled on them.
aws_arczonal_shift_zonal_autoshift_confi: `aws_arczonal_shift_zonal_autoshift_configuration` enables ARC zonal autoshift for a resource, letting AWS automatically and safely shift its traffic away from an Availability Zone the moment AWS itself detects a potential impairment there, ahead of the caller noticing anything.
aws_athena_capacity_reservation: `aws_athena_capacity_reservation` reserves dedicated Data Processing Units for Athena queries at a fixed price, an alternative to Athena's standard pay-per-data-scanned model, with one or more `aws_athena_work_group`s assigned to the reservation so their queries run on guaranteed capacity instead of queuing behind other tenants.
aws_athena_data_catalog: `aws_athena_data_catalog` registers a metadata catalog, the AWS Glue Data Catalog, a Hive metastore, or a federated Lambda-backed source, that Athena queries against to resolve which tables and schemas a SQL query can actually see.
aws_athena_work_group: `aws_athena_work_group` isolates a set of Athena users, teams, or applications, with its own query history, data usage limits, and encryption settings, so cost and access can be tracked and controlled per workgroup rather than pooled across every Athena user in the account.
aws_audit_manager_assessment: `aws_audit_manager_assessment` creates from an `aws_audit_manager_assessment_framework` the actual, running evidence-collection process, scoped to specific AWS accounts, that continuously gathers audit-ready evidence until the assessment is marked inactive. AWS Audit Manager is no longer open to new customers; existing customers can continue using it as normal.
aws_audit_manager_assessment_framework: `aws_audit_manager_assessment_framework` is a structured collection of controls, prebuilt for standards like PCI DSS, HIPAA, or SOC 2, or built custom, that an `aws_audit_manager_assessment` is created from to define exactly what evidence gets collected and against which requirements.
aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group: `aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group` creates a collection of EC2 instances managed as a single logical unit, with a minimum, maximum, and desired capacity that EC2 Auto Scaling enforces automatically, replacing unhealthy instances and balancing capacity across Availability Zones.
aws_auto_scaling_plans_scaling_plan: `aws_auto_scaling_plans_scaling_plan` combines target tracking and predictive scaling into one set of instructions applied across a tagged or CloudFormation-scoped group of resources, generating the real, underlying scaling policies on the caller's behalf from a single higher-level strategy like optimize-for-cost or optimize-for-availability.
aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy: `aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy` defines the condition under which an `aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group` launches or terminates instances, target tracking, step scaling, or predictive scaling against historical load, real logic a group has none of on its own beyond its static min/max/desired bounds.
aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool: `aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool` keeps a pool of pre-initialized EC2 instances attached to an `aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group` in a stopped or running state outside the group's own capacity count, so a scale-out event can pull an already-booted instance into service instead of waiting on a cold launch.
aws_b2_bi_capability: `aws_b2_bi_capability` connects an `aws_b2_bi_transformer` to specific Amazon S3 input and output locations, automating the processing workflow, EDI document arrives, gets transformed, lands in S3, that an `aws_b2_bi_partnership` then references.
aws_b2_bi_partnership: `aws_b2_bi_partnership` represents the actual trading relationship with a business partner, tying together an `aws_b2_bi_profile` and one or more `aws_b2_bi_capability` resources into the configuration AWS B2B Data Interchange uses to exchange documents with that specific partner correctly.
aws_b2_bi_profile: `aws_b2_bi_profile` stores an organization's own business contact information in AWS B2B Data Interchange, the foundation every `aws_b2_bi_partnership` is built on, since a partnership always ties a profile to a trading partner's capability.
aws_b2_bi_transformer: `aws_b2_bi_transformer` defines the mapping logic AWS B2B Data Interchange uses to convert EDI documents (X12, EDIFACT, HL7v2) to and from JSON or XML, the actual transformation a `aws_b2_bi_capability` then connects to real S3 input and output locations.
aws_backup_framework: `aws_backup_framework` is a set of built-in, customizable AWS Backup Audit Manager controls, aligned to an organization's own compliance requirements, that automatically track backup activity and flag resources not yet compliant with those controls.
aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor: `aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor` connects AWS Backup to an on-premises or VMware Cloud on AWS hypervisor through a deployed gateway appliance, letting AWS Backup discover, snapshot, and restore real virtual machines through vCenter Server without them ever needing to be natively AWS resources.
aws_backup_legal_hold: `aws_backup_legal_hold` places one or more real backups under an indefinite hold that blocks deletion and pauses any lifecycle transition that would remove them, until a user with sufficient permissions releases it, the mechanism AWS Backup provides for litigation and compliance retention that overrides a plan's own lifecycle rules.
aws_backup_logically_air_gapped_backup_v: `aws_backup_logically_air_gapped_backup_vault` stores backups in an isolated, service-owned account, locked by default and encrypted with AWS-owned keys, real protection against ransomware that specifically targets and deletes an account's own backup data, without requiring a separate copy of every backup to achieve it.
aws_backup_plan: `aws_backup_plan` defines a backup policy, schedule, lifecycle, and target `aws_backup_vault`, that gets applied to AWS resources through an `aws_backup_selection`, the real, centrally managed alternative to writing custom per-service backup scripts.
aws_backup_report_plan: `aws_backup_report_plan` generates recurring, downloadable AWS Backup Audit Manager reports summarizing compliance against an `aws_backup_framework`'s controls over time, real evidence a caller can hand to an auditor rather than assembling one by hand.
aws_backup_restore_testing_plan: `aws_backup_restore_testing_plan` schedules AWS Backup to automatically restore a sample of real recovery points on a recurring basis and validate the restore succeeded, catching a broken or unrestorable backup before an actual disaster does, rather than trusting an untested backup plan.
aws_backup_restore_testing_selection: `aws_backup_restore_testing_selection` picks which real recovery points and target resources an `aws_backup_restore_testing_plan` actually restores during a test run, the selection a restore testing plan has no scope without.
aws_backup_selection: `aws_backup_selection` assigns real AWS resources, by tag, by explicit resource ID, or by IAM role, to an `aws_backup_plan`, the actual mechanism that determines which resources a plan's schedule and lifecycle rules apply to. A plan with no selection protects nothing.
aws_backup_tiering_configuration: `aws_backup_tiering_configuration` automatically moves backup data in an `aws_backup_vault` to a lower-cost storage tier once it reaches a defined age (60 days minimum), while keeping identical restore capability, real, ongoing storage savings without the caller managing the transition by hand.
aws_backup_vault: `aws_backup_vault` is where AWS Backup actually stores backups, separated from their source resources so a backup survives even if the original EC2 instance or EBS volume is deleted, with its own encryption key and resource-based access policy controlling who can read or restore from it.
aws_batch_compute_environment: `aws_batch_compute_environment` provisions the real compute, EC2, Fargate, or Spot, that AWS Batch runs jobs on, managed or unmanaged, the layer an `aws_batch_job_queue` submits work into once a job is scheduled.
aws_batch_consumable_resource: `aws_batch_consumable_resource` defines a real constraint beyond vCPU, GPU, or memory, a third-party license token pool, a database connection limit, an API rate cap, that AWS Batch's resource-aware scheduling checks before starting a job, so a job doesn't launch, consume compute time, and then fail discovering the real resource it needed was unavailable.
aws_batch_job_definition: `aws_batch_job_definition` is the real template AWS Batch launches a job from, the container image, vCPU and memory requirements, command, and retry strategy, submitted against an `aws_batch_job_queue` each time a job actually runs.
aws_batch_job_queue: `aws_batch_job_queue` holds submitted jobs until an `aws_batch_compute_environment` has capacity to run them, ordered either FIFO by default or by an attached `aws_batch_scheduling_policy`'s fair-share rules across multiple users or workloads.
aws_batch_scheduling_policy: `aws_batch_scheduling_policy` defines fair-share scheduling for an `aws_batch_job_queue`, assigning share identifiers, decay time, and weight factors so one user or workload can't monopolize a queue's compute, real logic a queue defaults to plain FIFO without.
aws_batch_service_environment: `aws_batch_service_environment` holds the SageMaker AI-specific configuration, including maximum concurrent training instances, that lets AWS Batch queue, schedule, and prioritize real SageMaker Training jobs using the same queuing engine it uses for containerized batch workloads.
aws_bcm_dashboard: `aws_bcm_dashboard` combines multiple real cost data visualizations, Cost Explorer, Savings Plans, and Reserved Instance metrics among them, into one shareable dashboard, built and permissioned programmatically rather than reassembled by hand each time in the console.
aws_bcm_pricing_calculator_bill_scenario: `aws_bcm_pricing_calculator_bill_scenario` models planned AWS usage and commitments, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, inside the AWS Pricing Calculator, generating a real estimated bill from actual discount and benefit-sharing preferences rather than a rough, unofficial estimate.
aws_bcmdata_exports_export: `aws_bcmdata_exports_export` defines a customized, recurring export from AWS's own cost and usage or cost-optimization-recommendation datasets, the real mechanism for getting billing data out of AWS Billing and Cost Management into a caller's own data warehouse or pipeline on a schedule.
aws_bedrock_agent: `aws_bedrock_agent` orchestrates a foundation model, instructions, action groups (API operations or Lambda functions the agent can invoke), and knowledge bases into an agent that interprets user input, decides what to call, and iterates until it can return a final response. Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Bedrock Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is its successor for new work.
aws_bedrock_agent_alias: `aws_bedrock_agent_alias` points at a specific prepared version of an `aws_bedrock_agent`, letting a caller roll back or run two versions side by side for testing without disrupting whatever's currently invoking the agent in production.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom` configures AgentCore's Browser tool with the caller's own network and access settings, giving an agent a real, isolated environment to interact with live websites at scale, beyond AgentCore's own default browser configuration.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_capacity_provider: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_capacity_provider` defines the EC2 infrastructure, operating system, instance types, VPC and subnets, storage, IAM roles, that AgentCore Runtime instances provision on, patch, and scale automatically, an alternative to the microVM-based runtime for agents that need persistent, dedicated compute.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_code_interpreter_: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_code_interpreter_custom` configures AgentCore's Code Interpreter with a caller's own network mode (sandboxed, public internet, or a specific VPC) and execution role, letting an agent write and run real Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript code with access scoped beyond AgentCore's own default isolated sandbox.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_dataset: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_dataset` is a fixed set of test scenarios AgentCore runs an agent against in one call, invoking it, waiting for telemetry, and scoring the results with an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_evaluator`, real regression testing for agent behavior instead of manually invoking and checking each scenario.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_evaluator: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_evaluator` scores an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness`'s real execution traces, built-in LLM-as-a-judge evaluators for helpfulness, faithfulness, and safety, or a caller's own custom evaluator, quantifying agent quality rather than relying on spot-checking transcripts by hand.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway` securely exposes and routes traffic to real tools, MCP servers, inference models, other agents, or plain HTTP endpoints, at scale, so agents discover and call tools through one governed entry point instead of each agent integrating with every tool directly.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rate_limi: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rate_limit` caps how much traffic, requests per second or minute, tokens per minute for inference, or concurrent connections, an individual user can consume through an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway`, fine-grained, per-caller control rather than one limit applied to the gateway as a whole.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rule: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rule` defines the OAuth- or IAM-based condition an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rate_limit` actually applies under, the real matching logic a rate limit's request, token, and connection caps are scoped by.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target` is one real MCP, inference, or HTTP-passthrough destination an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway` routes traffic to, the actual tool or endpoint behind the gateway's own single entry point.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness` defines an agent with a single CreateHarness call and runs it with a single InvokeHarness call, AgentCore's fastest path from an agent definition to a running one, without separately wiring runtime, gateway, and memory resources by hand.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory` gives an agent both short-term memory, turn-by-turn context within one session, and long-term memory, retained knowledge across sessions, so it holds context and personalization without the caller building and managing their own memory store.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_oauth2_credential: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_oauth2_credential_provider` configures AgentCore Identity to obtain and store OAuth 2.0 tokens, user-delegated or machine-to-machine, from an external authorization server, with a unique callback URL per provider to bind a session and prevent cross-provider replay, real credential management an agent doesn't otherwise have to build itself.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_online_evaluation: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_online_evaluation_config` defines which `aws_bedrock_agent_core_evaluator`s run continuously against live agent sessions as they happen, real, ongoing quality scoring in production rather than only at test time.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_connector: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_connector` integrates an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_manager` with one real external payment provider, Coinbase or Stripe, for instance, referencing a credential stored in AgentCore Identity so API keys and wallet secrets are never passed directly through the Payments API.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_manager: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_manager` is the top-level AgentCore Payments resource for an AWS account, provisioning a real workload identity in AgentCore Identity and coordinating every payment operation run through it.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime` is the secure, serverless environment AgentCore hosts an agent or tool in, packaging the caller's code into a container image, pushing it to ECR, and deploying it, without the caller managing any of that infrastructure directly.
aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime_endpoint: `aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime_endpoint` is a stable, versioned entry point for invoking an `aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime`, letting a caller manage and route to different runtime configurations by ARN rather than a single, unversioned invocation target.
aws_bedrock_application_inference_profil: `aws_bedrock_application_inference_profile` defines a foundation model and the Region or Regions its invocation requests can route to, giving Amazon Bedrock a real, trackable identity to attach CloudWatch usage metrics and cost allocation to, separate from tracking usage against the underlying model ID directly.
aws_bedrock_automated_reasoning_policy: `aws_bedrock_automated_reasoning_policy` encodes a domain expert's own rules, an operational workflow, an HR policy, into a formal specification that Amazon Bedrock Guardrails checks a model's response against using real mathematical logic, not another model's judgment, to catch hallucinations and unstated assumptions with a provable, not probabilistic, guarantee.
aws_bedrock_data_automation_library: `aws_bedrock_data_automation_library` stores domain-specific entities and, currently, custom vocabulary that improve Bedrock Data Automation's extraction accuracy for audio and video content once associated with an `aws_bedrock_data_automation_project`, applied automatically to every job that project runs without per-job configuration.
aws_bedrock_data_automation_project: `aws_bedrock_data_automation_project` configures how Bedrock Data Automation extracts structured insights, text, tables, entities, from unstructured documents, images, audio, and video, the real container jobs run through and that an `aws_bedrock_data_automation_library` can be associated with.
aws_bedrock_data_source: `aws_bedrock_data_source` connects an `aws_bedrock_knowledge_base` to where its real content actually lives, S3, Confluence, SharePoint, Salesforce, or a web source, the ingestion point a knowledge base has nothing to retrieve from without.
aws_bedrock_flow: `aws_bedrock_flow` visually links multiple foundation models, prompts, and AWS services into one generative AI workflow in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows, reducing what would otherwise be custom orchestration code to a defined graph of connected nodes.
aws_bedrock_flow_alias: `aws_bedrock_flow_alias` points at a specific `aws_bedrock_flow_version`, letting a caller roll back a flow or A/B test two versions without changing whatever's invoking the flow by its alias.
aws_bedrock_flow_version: `aws_bedrock_flow_version` snapshots an `aws_bedrock_flow`'s definition at a point in time, the real, immutable target an `aws_bedrock_flow_alias` actually points to and invokes.
aws_bedrock_guardrail: `aws_bedrock_guardrail` configures real, runtime content filters, hate, insults, sexual content, violence, prompt-attack detection among them, plus PII masking, applied to both input prompts and model responses, with a configurable block action when Amazon Bedrock detects harmful content.
aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router: `aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router` predicts, per request, which model in a family is likely to give an acceptable response at the lowest cost, and routes the request there automatically, sending easier prompts to a cheaper model and harder ones to a more capable one without the caller choosing per call.
aws_bedrock_knowledge_base: `aws_bedrock_knowledge_base` is Amazon Bedrock's managed Retrieval Augmented Generation capability, converting ingested documents into vector embeddings in a real vector store (OpenSearch Serverless by default, or Aurora, Neptune Analytics, MongoDB, Pinecone, and others), so an `aws_bedrock_agent` or a direct query can retrieve relevant context to ground a model's response in real data rather than its training alone.
aws_bedrock_prompt: `aws_bedrock_prompt` stores a reusable prompt template in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management, created, evaluated, and shared through the console or API rather than hardcoded into application code, so the same tested prompt can be reused across an application.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version: `aws_bedrock_prompt_version` snapshots an `aws_bedrock_prompt`'s content at a point in time, the real, versioned target that gets deployed and referenced once a prompt has been tested and is ready for production use.
aws_bedrock_session: `aws_bedrock_session` persists conversation state and context across multiple, separate Amazon Bedrock invocations, the managed alternative to a caller building and scaling their own backend to checkpoint multi-step generative AI conversations built with frameworks like LangGraph or LlamaIndex.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group: `aws_billing_conductor_billing_group` is a set of accounts (or AWS Organizations, for billing-transfer customers) sharing one primary account and one pricing plan in AWS Billing Conductor, the unit a custom, pro forma version of AWS billing data is actually generated and charged back against.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item: `aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item` adds a manually defined charge or credit, a flat fee, a support markup, a negotiated discount, into an `aws_billing_conductor_billing_group`'s pro forma cost data, alongside its real, pricing-plan-derived AWS costs.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan: `aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan` bundles one or more `aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule`s into the pricing an `aws_billing_conductor_billing_group`'s member accounts see, letting an organization define custom, marked-up, or discounted rates for chargeback and showback separate from AWS's own real bill.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule: `aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule` defines one global or service-specific rate adjustment inside an `aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan`, the real building block a pricing plan combines several of to produce the rate an end customer actually sees.
aws_billing_view: `aws_billing_view` defines a segment of AWS cost and usage data, either the account's own default primary view or a custom, filtered view built and shared, via AWS Resource Access Manager, with other accounts so they see only the cost data the view's filter actually exposes.
aws_braket_spending_limit: `aws_braket_spending_limit` caps real, cumulative spend on Amazon Braket's on-demand and hybrid-job quantum processing unit tasks, validating every task creation request against the configured limit and rejecting it outright if its estimated cost would exceed what remains, with an optional time window scoping when submissions are even allowed.
aws_budgets_budget: `aws_budgets_budget` tracks real AWS cost, usage, Reserved Instance utilization/coverage, or Savings Plans utilization/coverage against a defined threshold, fixed or growing, and can notify by email or SNS when actual or forecasted spend crosses it.
aws_budgets_budgets_action: `aws_budgets_budgets_action` attaches a real, automatic response, applying an IAM policy that denies further provisioning, for instance, to an `aws_budgets_budget` crossing its threshold, turning a budget from a passive alert into an enforced spending control.
aws_cases_case: `aws_cases_case` is one real case record created from an `aws_cases_template` inside an `aws_cases_domain`, holding whatever field values that template defines, and evaluated against any `aws_cases_case_rule`s configured for the domain.
aws_cases_case_rule: `aws_cases_case_rule` automatically runs whenever an `aws_cases_case` is created or updated, matching conditions like a field value, a priority, or an SLA breach, and taking a real action, assigning an SLA, creating a task, sending an alert, without an agent doing it by hand.
aws_cases_domain: `aws_cases_domain` is the container for all Connect Cases data in one Amazon Connect instance, cases, `aws_cases_field`s, `aws_cases_layout`s, and `aws_cases_template`s all live inside exactly one domain, and an instance can be associated with only one.
aws_cases_field: `aws_cases_field` defines one piece of data a case can capture, a system field or a custom one, with its own declared data type, created inside an `aws_cases_case` domain and referenced by ID from an `aws_cases_template`.
aws_cases_layout: `aws_cases_layout` organizes how an `aws_cases_case`'s fields are actually displayed to an agent, working together with an `aws_cases_template`, which combines a layout with a set of fields into one reusable case structure.
aws_cases_template: `aws_cases_template` defines a case's object model, which `aws_cases_field`s it captures and which `aws_cases_layout` displays them, referencing both by ID, so every case created from the template shares the same real structure.
aws_cassandra_keyspace: `aws_cassandra_keyspace` creates the top-level namespace in Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra), the serverless, Cassandra-compatible database, that every `aws_cassandra_table` and user-defined `aws_cassandra_type` in it belongs to.
aws_cassandra_table: `aws_cassandra_table` creates a real table inside an `aws_cassandra_keyspace`, using the same CQL data model and application code an existing Cassandra workload already uses, with Amazon Keyspaces scaling its throughput and storage automatically rather than the caller provisioning nodes.
aws_cassandra_type: `aws_cassandra_type` is a user-defined type, a named grouping of fields and data types usable as a single column, created inside an `aws_cassandra_keyspace` with CQL's `CREATE TYPE` and available to every `aws_cassandra_table` in that same keyspace.
aws_ce_anomaly_monitor: `aws_ce_anomaly_monitor` watches spend segmented by AWS service, linked account, cost allocation tag, or `aws_ce_cost_category`, using machine learning to detect unusual patterns against that segment's own normal spend, the real detection engine an `aws_ce_anomaly_subscription`'s alerts are triggered by.
aws_ce_anomaly_subscription: `aws_ce_anomaly_subscription` attaches real alert recipients and a notification channel to an `aws_ce_anomaly_monitor`, the actual delivery mechanism a monitor's own detected anomalies have no way to reach anyone without.
aws_ce_cost_category: `aws_ce_cost_category` groups AWS costs by custom, rule-based categories, mapping accounts, tags, or services into a caller's own real business dimensions, engineering versus marketing spend, for instance, so Cost Explorer and cost anomaly monitors can analyze and alert on those groupings directly rather than only on AWS's native billing dimensions.
aws_certificate_manager_account: `aws_certificate_manager_account` configures account-wide ACM settings, specifically how many days before expiry ACM starts sending daily EventBridge events for every `aws_certificate_manager_certificate` in the account, 45 days by default for private and imported certificates, 30 for public ones.
aws_certificate_manager_certificate: `aws_certificate_manager_certificate` issues or imports a public or private SSL/TLS X.509 certificate for one or more domain names, wildcards included, that ACM then renews automatically for services issued directly through it, a certificate is a regional resource and can't be copied between Regions.
aws_chatbot_custom_action: `aws_chatbot_custom_action` defines a configurable button, running a CLI command, a Lambda function, or an SSM Automation runbook, that appears on an AWS event notification in Slack or Microsoft Teams, letting a channel operationalize a real incident-response or DevOps action directly from the notification rather than switching to the console.
aws_chatbot_microsoft_teams_channel_conf: `aws_chatbot_microsoft_teams_channel_configuration` connects a Microsoft Teams channel to AWS Chatbot, the Teams counterpart to `aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration`, with its own real team and tenant ID, SNS topics, IAM role, and guardrail policies.
aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration: `aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration` connects a Slack channel to AWS Chatbot, real SNS topics for notification delivery, an IAM role Chatbot assumes, and optional IAM policy guardrails restricting what commands can run from that channel.
aws_chime_app_instance: `aws_chime_app_instance` creates the top-level messaging container in Amazon Chime SDK Identity, the real resource every `aws_chime_app_instance_user` and `aws_chime_app_instance_bot` for a messaging application belongs to.
aws_chime_app_instance_bot: `aws_chime_app_instance_bot` registers an automated, non-human participant inside an `aws_chime_app_instance`, able to send and receive channel messages the same way an `aws_chime_app_instance_user` does, the real identity behind an AI or automated assistant integrated into Chime SDK messaging.
aws_chime_app_instance_user: `aws_chime_app_instance_user` registers a real, addressable participant, typically created the first time a person signs in, inside an `aws_chime_app_instance`, the identity that Chime SDK messaging attaches as the sender of a message or the member of a channel.
aws_chime_channel_flow: `aws_chime_channel_flow` defines an ordered sequence of processors, Lambda functions among them, that Chime SDK messaging invokes on a message before it's delivered to a channel, the real mechanism for moderation, translation, or other automated processing applied consistently to every message sent.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template: `aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template` pre-approves the exact SQL query or PySpark job a collaboration will allow, agreed on in advance by collaboration members so what analysis can run is fixed and reviewed rather than left open to whatever a member decides to query later.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration: `aws_clean_rooms_collaboration` creates the actual secure workspace multiple AWS accounts join to analyze their combined data, inviting partner accounts and setting the privacy-enhancing controls that govern what any one party can see of another's underlying data.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table: `aws_clean_rooms_configured_table` links a real S3, Athena, Glue, or Snowflake data source into AWS Clean Rooms with an attached analysis rule restricting what SQL queries can run against it, so a collaboration member's raw data is queryable under real, enforced constraints rather than exposed directly.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa: `aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_association` associates an `aws_clean_rooms_configured_table` with a specific `aws_clean_rooms_membership`, the actual grant that makes a configured table usable within one collaboration rather than just configured in the abstract.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table: `aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table` performs real entity resolution inside AWS Clean Rooms, matching records that represent the same real-world entity across two collaboration members' data, integrated with AWS Entity Resolution, without either party seeing the other's raw identifiers.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association: `aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association` associates an AWS Entity Resolution ID namespace with an `aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table`, the real link that makes a namespace's own resolved identities usable for matching inside a specific Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table: `aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table` stores the real, intermediate output of a multi-step Clean Rooms analysis, populated by one query and then queryable by a further, real analysis rule of its own, rather than every step needing to reprocess from each member's original configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_membership: `aws_clean_rooms_membership` is the real resource an invited AWS account creates to actually join an `aws_clean_rooms_collaboration` it's been invited to, distinct from the collaboration itself, which only the creating account manages directly.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo: `aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algorithm` makes a container training image available for use inside AWS Clean Rooms ML, the real, deployable model logic an `aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset` gets trained against without either collaboration member sharing raw training data with the other.

`aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algorithm_association` associates an `aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algorithm` with a specific collaboration membership, the real grant that makes a configured algorithm usable inside one collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset: `aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset` points AWS Clean Rooms ML at the real AWS Glue table, and its user, item, and timestamp columns, used to train a lookalike model, Clean Rooms ML reads metadata about the location rather than copying the underlying training data itself.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template: `aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template` defines the real, mathematically-backed differential privacy budget, how much cumulative query exposure is allowed before results get too noisy to protect individual users, that AWS Clean Rooms enforces automatically across a collaboration's differential-privacy-protected queries.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2: `aws_cloud9_environment_ec2` provisions an EC2-backed Cloud9 IDE environment, a browser-based development environment with a real EC2 instance behind it. AWS Cloud9 is no longer available to new customers as of July 25, 2024; AWS recommends AWS IDE Toolkits and AWS CloudShell going forward, with existing Cloud9 customers able to continue using the service as normal.
aws_cloud_formation_custom_resource: `aws_cloud_formation_custom_resource` runs a caller's own real logic, typically a Lambda function, as part of an `aws_cloud_formation_stack`'s create, update, and delete lifecycle, letting a stack manage something CloudFormation itself has no native resource type for.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook: `aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook` implements a CloudFormation Hook using AWS CloudFormation Guard's declarative, policy-as-code rules instead of a Lambda function, the same real pre-provisioning compliance check as an `aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook` written without general-purpose code.
aws_cloud_formation_hook_version: `aws_cloud_formation_hook_version` is a specific, registered version of a custom Hook extension, an `aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook` or `aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook`, in the CloudFormation registry, the real mechanism that lets a Hook's own logic be updated and rolled out without breaking stacks already relying on an earlier version.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook: `aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook` implements a CloudFormation Hook, real, custom code that inspects a resource's configuration before it's provisioned and either blocks or warns on non-compliant configurations, using a Lambda function to run the actual evaluation logic in any Lambda-supported language.
aws_cloud_formation_macro: `aws_cloud_formation_macro` registers real, custom template-processing logic, invoked via a template's Transform section or the `Fn::Transform` intrinsic function, that CloudFormation runs against a template or template fragment before creating a stack from it, anything from a simple find-and-replace to a full template rewrite.
aws_cloud_formation_resource_version: `aws_cloud_formation_resource_version` is a specific, registered version of a custom resource type in the CloudFormation registry, the real mechanism that versions a private or third-party extension's own schema and provisioning logic independently of any stack that uses it.
aws_cloud_formation_stack: `aws_cloud_formation_stack` is CloudFormation's own fundamental unit, a collection of AWS resources managed together as one, created, updated, and deleted as a single operation from a real template.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set: `aws_cloud_formation_stack_set` deploys the same `aws_cloud_formation_stack` template consistently across many AWS accounts and Regions from one operation, the real mechanism for organization-wide infrastructure rollout rather than manually repeating a stack deployment account by account.
aws_cloud_formation_type_activation: `aws_cloud_formation_type_activation` activates a public third-party extension, a resource type or module, from the CloudFormation registry for use in an account and Region's own stack templates, with real control over which major and minor version updates apply automatically.
aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition: `aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition` pauses an `aws_cloud_formation_stack`'s creation until it receives a real success signal, or times out, from an external process, the mechanism for coordinating stack creation with configuration work that happens outside CloudFormation itself.
aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition_handl: `aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition_handle` generates the real, pre-signed URL an external process signals success or failure to, referenced by an `aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition`'s own Handle property. AWS now recommends a stack resource's CreationPolicy attribute over this mechanism for new templates.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list: `aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list` reserves a real, static set of Anycast IP addresses (up to 21) dedicated to an account, that an `aws_cloud_front_distribution` can be assigned so viewers, network providers, or outbound firewalls can allowlist a fixed, known set of IPs instead of CloudFront's normal, dynamically assigned address space.
aws_cloud_front_cache_policy: `aws_cloud_front_cache_policy` defines what values, headers, cookies, query strings, CloudFront includes in its real cache key for an `aws_cloud_front_distribution`, determining what counts as the same cached object versus a cache miss requiring a fresh origin fetch.
aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_acces: `aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_access_identity` is CloudFront's original, legacy mechanism for restricting a private S3 origin to CloudFront-only access, a special CloudFront-managed identity granted read permission on the bucket. AWS now recommends `aws_cloud_front_origin_access_control` for new distributions.
aws_cloud_front_connection_function: `aws_cloud_front_connection_function` is a specialized `aws_cloud_front_function` that runs during the TLS handshake of a mutual TLS connection rather than against a viewer HTTP request, with access to client certificate details and revocation-check results for custom certificate validation logic like organizational-unit checks or IP-based certificate policy.
aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_po: `aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_policy` routes a real, configurable percentage of an `aws_cloud_front_distribution`'s production traffic to a staging distribution, letting a configuration change be tested against live traffic and incrementally rolled out before it fully replaces the primary distribution's own configuration.
aws_cloud_front_distribution: `aws_cloud_front_distribution` is the real, top-level CloudFront resource, telling CloudFront which origin (an S3 bucket, a custom HTTP server, and similar) to pull content from and how to cache and deliver it from edge locations worldwide.
aws_cloud_front_distribution_tenant: `aws_cloud_front_distribution_tenant` is the real, routable front door for one tenant's domain in CloudFront's multi-tenant distribution model (CloudFront SaaS Manager). The multi-tenant distribution it belongs to has no domain name of its own; only its distribution tenants are actually reachable by viewers.
aws_cloud_front_function: `aws_cloud_front_function` runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations against viewer requests and responses, URL rewrites, header manipulation, simple validation, with submillisecond startup, cheaper and faster than Lambda@Edge for logic that doesn't need a full Lambda runtime.
aws_cloud_front_key_group: `aws_cloud_front_key_group` holds one or more `aws_cloud_front_public_key`s that CloudFront validates signed URLs or signed cookies against, the real, required grouping an `aws_cloud_front_distribution`'s trusted-signer configuration references rather than a bare public key directly.
aws_cloud_front_key_value_store: `aws_cloud_front_key_value_store` is a globally replicated, low-latency key-value datastore an `aws_cloud_front_function` reads from at the edge, letting a function's data, an allowlist, an A/B test assignment, be updated independently of redeploying the function's own code.
aws_cloud_front_origin_access_control: `aws_cloud_front_origin_access_control` lets an `aws_cloud_front_distribution` sign its own requests to a private S3 bucket or other supported origin, so the origin can be restricted to CloudFront-only access, the current, real replacement for the older `aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_access_identity` mechanism.
aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy: `aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy` defines what values, headers, cookies, query strings, CloudFront actually forwards to the origin on a cache miss, kept separate from an `aws_cloud_front_cache_policy` so what's cached and what's sent to origin can be controlled independently.
aws_cloud_front_public_key: `aws_cloud_front_public_key` registers the real public half of a signing key pair with CloudFront, used inside an `aws_cloud_front_key_group` to validate signed URLs and signed cookies for private content.
aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config: `aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config` streams an `aws_cloud_front_distribution`'s access logs to Kinesis Data Streams within seconds of each request, real-time visibility into edge traffic rather than the batched, delayed delivery of CloudFront's standard access logs.
aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy: `aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy` adds or overrides real HTTP response headers, CORS, security headers among them, on every response an `aws_cloud_front_distribution` returns, without the origin itself needing to set them.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution: `aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution` is CloudFront's legacy RTMP media-streaming distribution type, a narrower, deprecated predecessor to the general-purpose `aws_cloud_front_distribution` that AWS has directed customers away from for years in favor of HTTP-based streaming.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store: `aws_cloud_front_trust_store` is the real repository of CA certificates an `aws_cloud_front_distribution` validates client certificates against during mutual TLS, defining which certificate authorities are trusted to have issued a valid client certificate.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin: `aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin` connects an `aws_cloud_front_distribution` directly to an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance in a private VPC subnet through an AWS-managed ENI, so the real origin never needs a public IP or to be reachable from the open internet at all.
aws_cloud_trail_channel: `aws_cloud_trail_channel` is the real integration point CloudTrail Lake uses to ingest events from an outside source, a CloudTrail partner integration or a caller's own application, into an `aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store` alongside native AWS activity.
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard: `aws_cloud_trail_dashboard` visualizes real, aggregated trends from an `aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store`, CloudTrail Lake's own built-in analytics view rather than a caller writing and re-running the underlying queries by hand each time.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store: `aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store` is an immutable, queryable collection of events in CloudTrail Lake, converted to columnar Apache ORC storage for fast retrieval and retained for up to 10 years, real, long-term audit data queried directly rather than exported and reprocessed elsewhere.
aws_cloud_trail_trail: `aws_cloud_trail_trail` captures AWS account activity as events and delivers them continuously to an S3 bucket, with optional delivery to CloudWatch Logs and EventBridge, the real, ongoing record of API calls across the console, CLI, and SDKs, as opposed to CloudTrail's own 90-day, no-setup-required Event history.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm: `aws_cloud_watch_alarm` watches a real CloudWatch metric against a defined threshold and changes state, triggering a notification or an automated action like an Auto Scaling adjustment, when the threshold is breached.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule: `aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule` automatically mutes up to 100 named `aws_cloud_watch_alarm`s' own actions, SNS notifications, Auto Scaling triggers, during a real, defined recurring or one-time window, planned maintenance, a deployment, without stopping the alarms themselves from evaluating and changing state.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector: `aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector` learns a real metric's normal pattern, including seasonal and trend behavior, and computes an expected value band an `aws_cloud_watch_alarm` can alarm against, catching deviations a fixed, static threshold would either miss or false-positive on.
aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm: `aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm` combines the state of multiple `aws_cloud_watch_alarm`s with a real boolean expression (AND, OR, NOT), alarming only on the actual combined condition rather than firing separately, and noisily, for every individual underlying alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_dashboard: `aws_cloud_watch_dashboard` is a real, customizable, unified visualization of metrics and logs, shareable across accounts and Regions, that a caller builds by hand or gets automatically curated for many AWS services without building one from scratch.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule: `aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule` is a Contributor Insights rule, a real, JSON-defined filter and aggregation run against log data to surface the top contributors, the noisiest client IPs, the slowest URLs, to a pattern rather than only an aggregate metric.
aws_cloud_watch_log_alarm: `aws_cloud_watch_log_alarm` runs a real CloudWatch Logs Insights query on a schedule and alarms when its aggregated results breach a threshold across a defined number of recent executions, catching patterns and error rates directly in log data without first building a metric filter to extract a number from it.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream: `aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream` continuously streams real, near real-time CloudWatch metric updates to a destination like Kinesis Data Firehose, an ongoing feed for a third-party observability tool rather than that tool polling the CloudWatch API on an interval.
aws_code_artifact_domain: `aws_code_artifact_domain` is CodeArtifact's top-level grouping for an organization's own package repositories, one production domain typically holding every `aws_code_artifact_repository` a company uses, so packages can be discovered and shared consistently across development teams.
aws_code_artifact_package_group: `aws_code_artifact_package_group` applies real origin control and configuration consistently across every package in an `aws_code_artifact_domain` whose name matches the group's pattern, rather than a caller setting the same policy on each individual package by hand.
aws_code_artifact_repository: `aws_code_artifact_repository` stores real software packages, polyglot by default, npm, Maven, PyPI, and others in the same repository, inside an `aws_code_artifact_domain`, either published directly or fetched on demand from a connected public repository like npmjs or Maven Central.
aws_code_build_fleet: `aws_code_build_fleet` reserves a real, persistent pool of CodeBuild compute hosts that stay warm and ready, cutting a build's startup latency versus CodeBuild's default on-demand provisioning, at the cost of paying for the fleet's capacity even while it's idle.
