aws_code_build_project: `aws_code_build_project` defines a real, fully managed build, its source, build environment, and buildspec, that AWS CodeBuild compiles, tests, and packages into deployable artifacts, run standalone or as a stage in an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline`.
aws_code_build_report_group: `aws_code_build_report_group` collects real test and code-coverage reports generated by an `aws_code_build_project`'s own builds into one place, so results across many build runs can be reviewed and trended together instead of inspected one build log at a time.
aws_code_commit_repository: `aws_code_commit_repository` creates a private, fully managed Git repository in AWS CodeCommit, encrypted at rest and in transit, supporting standard Git commands and tools. AWS CodeCommit stopped onboarding new customers on July 25, 2024; existing customers with a repository can continue creating additional ones and using the service as normal.
aws_code_connections_connection: `aws_code_connections_connection` links AWS to an external source provider, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, once authorized, so a real `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` or other AWS service can pull code without re-authenticating per use. AWS CodeConnections is the March 2024 rename of AWS CodeStar Connections; the older `aws_code_star_connections_connection` resource type continues to work.
aws_code_deploy_application: `aws_code_deploy_application` is CodeDeploy's own top-level container name, ensuring the correct combination of revision, `aws_code_deploy_deployment_config`, and `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` gets referenced together each time a real deployment runs.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config: `aws_code_deploy_deployment_config` defines the real rollout pace an `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` deploys with, one instance at a time, half at a time, or all at once, among CodeDeploy's predefined configs, or a custom one.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group: `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` is the real, specific set of EC2 instances, an Auto Scaling group, or an ECS service and load balancer, that an `aws_code_deploy_application`'s revisions actually get deployed to, along with when to reroute traffic and when to retire the old version.
aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group: `aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group` is the real unit CodeGuru Profiler aggregates and analyzes application performance data under, one or more applications' profiling agents all reporting into the same group so performance issues can be identified across them together rather than per application.
aws_code_guru_reviewer_repository_associ: `aws_code_guru_reviewer_repository_association` connects a real source repository to Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer for automated code review. As of November 7, 2025, CodeGuru Reviewer is in maintenance mode and closed to new repository associations; existing associations continue working, with Amazon Q Developer's own code review capabilities positioned as the real successor.
aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type: `aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type` defines a caller's own real action an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` stage can invoke, beyond CodePipeline's built-in source, build, test, and deploy actions, for integrating a tool AWS doesn't provide a native action for.
aws_code_pipeline_pipeline: `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` models the real, automated stages, source, build, test, deploy, that a code change moves through on its way to release, the core, top-level resource every other CodePipeline resource attaches to.
aws_code_pipeline_webhook: `aws_code_pipeline_webhook` triggers an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` execution the moment a real external event happens, a GitHub push, for instance, rather than the pipeline polling its source on an interval to notice a change.
aws_code_star_connections_connection: `aws_code_star_connections_connection` is the pre-rename CloudFormation resource type for what's now `aws_code_connections_connection`, AWS CodeStar Connections having been renamed AWS CodeConnections in March 2024. Existing connections and this resource type continue to work; the old APIs stopped being available after April 2025.
aws_code_star_connections_repository_lin: `aws_code_star_connections_repository_link` ties a real, specific repository to an `aws_code_star_connections_connection`, a persistent reference CodePipeline's V2 pipeline types and other AWS services use for source actions rather than resolving the repository from the connection alone each time.
aws_code_star_git_hub_repository: `aws_code_star_git_hub_repository` creates a GitHub repository as part of the original AWS CodeStar service's own project setup. AWS discontinued creating and viewing CodeStar projects on July 31, 2024; resources CodeStar already created, including this repository, its source repos, pipelines, and builds, continue functioning unaffected.
aws_code_star_notifications_notification: `aws_code_star_notifications_notification_rule` sends real notifications, to Slack via AWS Chatbot, to SNS, to email, when a specific event happens in a CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, or CodePipeline resource. Despite the shared name, this service was unaffected by CodeStar's own 2024 discontinuation and remains active.
aws_cognito_identity_pool: `aws_cognito_identity_pool` issues real, temporary AWS credentials, via AWS STS, to authenticated or guest users, accepting claims from an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, a SAML 2.0 provider, or a social identity provider, independent of whether a user pool is used alongside it.
aws_cognito_identity_pool_principal_tag: `aws_cognito_identity_pool_principal_tag` maps an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`'s real claims from one specific identity provider into IAM principal tags on a user's temporary AWS STS session, enabling attribute-based access control policies keyed on those tags.
aws_cognito_identity_pool_role_attachmen: `aws_cognito_identity_pool_role_attachment` maps real IAM roles to an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`, by default role, by rules against a user's claims, or by their `aws_cognito_user_pool_group` membership, the actual configuration that determines which role a user gets credentials for.
aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration: `aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration` routes an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s own real audit and activity logs, sign-in events, user notifications, by event source and log level, to a specific CloudWatch Logs log group, rather than that activity going unrecorded outside CloudTrail's own API-call logging.
aws_cognito_managed_login_branding: `aws_cognito_managed_login_branding` applies real visual branding, logo, colors, layout, to an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s managed login pages through a no-code visual editor or a large set of programmatic style options, rather than every sign-in page looking like Cognito's own unbranded default.
aws_cognito_terms: `aws_cognito_terms` configures real terms of use and privacy policy document links for an `aws_cognito_user_pool_client`, shown on managed login's sign-up page in the language matching the user's own locale, with a defined fallback when no localized document exists.
aws_cognito_user_pool: `aws_cognito_user_pool` is a real, standalone user directory and OIDC identity provider, sign-up, sign-in, and federation with third-party IdPs, that issues JWTs directly to an app, independent of whether an `aws_cognito_identity_pool` is ever used alongside it.
aws_cognito_user_pool_client: `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` registers a real, specific application, a web app, a mobile app, a backend service, against an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, with its own allowed OAuth flows, callback URLs, and token settings, the actual identity a caller authenticates as when it talks to the user pool.
aws_cognito_user_pool_domain: `aws_cognito_user_pool_domain` hosts an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s real managed login pages, either a Cognito-provided prefix domain or a custom domain, the authorization and web server that federated and local sign-in actually happens through.
aws_cognito_user_pool_group: `aws_cognito_user_pool_group` creates a real, logical grouping of users inside an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, listed in the ID and access tokens Cognito issues, and usable to map a user to a specific IAM role when a token is passed to an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`.
aws_cognito_user_pool_identity_provider: `aws_cognito_user_pool_identity_provider` federates an `aws_cognito_user_pool` with a real external identity source, Google, Facebook, SAML 2.0, or another OIDC provider, mapping that provider's claims into the standardized JWT the user pool issues to an app.
aws_cognito_user_pool_regional_configura: `aws_cognito_user_pool_regional_configuration_attachment` configures an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s real, Region-specific settings, including its email delivery configuration, SES sender address, configuration set, distinct from the user pool's own core identity and authentication settings.
aws_cognito_user_pool_replica: `aws_cognito_user_pool_replica` creates a real, secondary copy of an `aws_cognito_user_pool` in another AWS Region for multi-Region failover, supporting a growing subset of authentication and session operations locally depending on whether the replica is active or inactive.
aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server: `aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server` defines a real API an `aws_cognito_user_pool` can issue OAuth access tokens scoped to, the mechanism behind machine-to-machine authorization and fine-grained API access control in Cognito rather than a single, undifferentiated access token.
aws_cognito_user_pool_risk_configuration: `aws_cognito_user_pool_risk_configuration_attachment` configures real adaptive authentication for an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, scoring each sign-in for risk based on IP address, device, and behavioral factors, and requiring extra MFA or blocking the attempt outright at higher risk levels.
aws_cognito_user_pool_uicustomization_at: `aws_cognito_user_pool_uicustomization_attachment` applies CSS and logo customization to an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s legacy Hosted UI (classic) sign-in pages, the older customization mechanism that `aws_cognito_managed_login_branding` supersedes for user pools on managed login.
aws_cognito_user_pool_user: `aws_cognito_user_pool_user` is a real, individual user record created directly inside an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, administrator-created rather than self-registered, with its own attributes and initial credential state.
aws_cognito_user_pool_user_to_group_atta: `aws_cognito_user_pool_user_to_group_attachment` is the real, actual membership grant linking an `aws_cognito_user_pool_user` to an `aws_cognito_user_pool_group`. Neither existing on its own makes a user a group member, this attachment does.
aws_comprehend_document_classifier: `aws_comprehend_document_classifier` trains a real, custom model on caller-labeled documents, plain text, PDF, Word, or images, to categorize new documents into the caller's own classes, single-label or multi-label, run synchronously in real time or as a batch job against a whole document set.
aws_comprehend_flywheel: `aws_comprehend_flywheel` orchestrates the continuous retraining of a custom Comprehend classification or entity-recognition model, storing every version's training and test data in a real, managed data lake, so a caller can add new labeled data periodically, run an iteration that evaluates and trains a new model version, and promote it once its metrics improve on the active version.
aws_compute_optimizer_automation_rule: `aws_compute_optimizer_automation_rule` automatically applies EBS volume optimization recommendations, cleaning up unattached volumes and upgrading to newer volume types, on a real recurring schedule against resources matching a Region or tag filter, with a dashboard tracking every automated action and estimated savings, and the ability to reverse one.
aws_config_config_rule: `aws_config_config_rule` evaluates a real AWS resource's configuration against a defined condition every time it's created, changed, or deleted, flagging the resource noncompliant and sending a notification the moment it violates the rule rather than requiring a caller to poll for drift.
aws_config_configuration_aggregator: `aws_config_configuration_aggregator` pulls real AWS Config configuration and compliance data from multiple accounts and Regions into one, centralized account and Region, so a caller gets one unified inventory and compliance view instead of checking each account and Region separately.
aws_config_configuration_recorder: `aws_config_configuration_recorder` is the real, account-level switch that determines whether and which resource types AWS Config actually records configuration and configuration history for, the foundational resource every other AWS Config capability, rules, aggregation, remediation, depends on being turned on.
aws_config_conformance_pack: `aws_config_conformance_pack` bundles a real collection of `aws_config_config_rule`s and remediation actions into one deployable, monitorable unit, so an entire compliance standard's worth of rules gets rolled out and tracked together instead of one rule at a time.
aws_config_delivery_channel: `aws_config_delivery_channel` tells AWS Config where to actually deliver what an `aws_config_configuration_recorder` records, a configuration snapshot and history to an S3 bucket, and change notifications to an SNS topic.
aws_config_organization_config_rule: `aws_config_organization_config_rule` deploys an `aws_config_config_rule` across every account in an AWS Organization at once, the org-wide counterpart to defining and rolling out the same rule to each member account individually.
aws_config_organization_conformance_pack: `aws_config_organization_conformance_pack` deploys an `aws_config_conformance_pack` across every account in an AWS Organization at once, the org-wide counterpart to rolling the same conformance pack out to each member account individually.
aws_config_remediation_configuration: `aws_config_remediation_configuration` defines the real, automated action, typically an SSM Automation document, AWS Config runs against a resource an `aws_config_config_rule` has flagged noncompliant, closing the loop from detection to an actual fix rather than only alerting on drift.
aws_config_stored_query: `aws_config_stored_query` saves a real, reusable SQL-like query against the current configuration state of AWS resources that AWS Config tracks, so a caller doesn't have to rewrite the same advanced query, security group rules open to 0.0.0.0/0, for instance, from scratch each time.
aws_connect_campaigns_campaign: `aws_connect_campaigns_campaign` defines a real, high-volume outbound campaign, appointment reminders, telemarketing, debt collection, run through an `aws_connect_instance`. Outbound Campaigns V1 isn't supported in every Region; `aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign` is the newer, multi-channel version AWS points new campaigns toward.
aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign: `aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign` is Outbound Campaigns V2, the real, actively developed successor to `aws_connect_campaigns_campaign` with multi-channel (voice, SMS, email, WhatsApp) and visual journey-builder support that V1 doesn't have.
aws_connect_contact_flow: `aws_connect_contact_flow` defines the real logic, IVR menus, routing decisions, Lambda invocations, that determines what happens to a contact, a call, a chat, a task, from the moment it enters an `aws_connect_instance` to the moment it's resolved.
aws_connect_contact_flow_module: `aws_connect_contact_flow_module` is a real, reusable block of logic that can be embedded inside multiple `aws_connect_contact_flow`s, so shared routing logic, a business-hours check, for instance, is maintained once rather than duplicated across every flow that needs it.
aws_connect_data_table: `aws_connect_data_table` is a real, no-code, JSON-like data structure an administrator manages directly, then reads from or writes to inside an `aws_connect_contact_flow` via the Data Table flow block, dynamic configuration, agent extension routing, seasonal messaging, that changes contact center behavior without a code deployment.
aws_connect_data_table_attribute: `aws_connect_data_table_attribute` defines one real column, its name and data type, in an `aws_connect_data_table`, the schema an `aws_connect_data_table_record` populates values against.
aws_connect_data_table_record: `aws_connect_data_table_record` is one real row of data in an `aws_connect_data_table`, the actual values a contact flow's Data Table block reads or writes at runtime.
aws_connect_email_address: `aws_connect_email_address` registers a real, dedicated email address an `aws_connect_instance` sends and receives customer email through, the email counterpart to a phone number for voice or an endpoint for chat.
aws_connect_evaluation_form: `aws_connect_evaluation_form` defines a real, weighted scorecard, sections and questions, used to grade a recorded or live contact, the structure Connect's own quality-management feature uses to produce a consistent, comparable score across every evaluation.
aws_connect_hours_of_operation: `aws_connect_hours_of_operation` defines a real, named schedule, open days and hours, that an `aws_connect_contact_flow` checks to route a contact differently outside business hours instead of every flow hardcoding its own time logic.
aws_connect_instance: `aws_connect_instance` provisions the real, top-level container for a contact center, telephony, chat, and every other Connect resource, agents, queues, contact flows, attaches to it. As of this session, AWS now uses "Amazon Connect" as the name of a broader portfolio of agentic business-function solutions, and refers to the contact center product this resource belongs to as "Amazon Connect Customer" (or simply Customer) in its own documentation, the two names used interchangeably during the transition.
aws_connect_instance_storage_config: `aws_connect_instance_storage_config` configures where an `aws_connect_instance` stores a specific category of real data, call recordings, chat transcripts, contact trace records, in S3, Kinesis, or Kinesis Firehose.
aws_connect_integration_association: `aws_connect_integration_association` connects an `aws_connect_instance` to a real, external third-party application through Amazon AppIntegrations, the mechanism behind third-party apps in the agent workspace and Amazon Q in Connect's own knowledge sources.
aws_connect_metric: `aws_connect_metric` defines a real, custom real-time or historical metric, built with advanced filters and functions on Connect's own metric primitives, for use in dashboards and the metrics API, beyond the fixed set of metrics Connect provides out of the box.
aws_connect_prompt: `aws_connect_prompt` registers a real, uploaded audio file as a named prompt an `aws_connect_contact_flow` can play back, IVR greetings, hold messages, configurable and reusable rather than referencing a raw audio file inline.
aws_connect_queue: `aws_connect_queue` holds real, waiting contacts until an agent, matched by an `aws_connect_routing_profile`, becomes available, the actual point contacts sit at between entering an `aws_connect_contact_flow` and being answered.
aws_connect_quick_connect: `aws_connect_quick_connect` creates a real, one-click transfer target for an agent, another queue, a specific user, or an external phone number, so a warm transfer or task assignment doesn't require dialing or searching for the destination each time.
aws_connect_routing_profile: `aws_connect_routing_profile` assigns an `aws_connect_user` to one or more `aws_connect_queue`s with real priority and channel concurrency settings, the mechanism that determines which queues an agent actually receives contacts from and how many at once.
aws_connect_rule: `aws_connect_rule` automates a real action, generating an EventBridge event, sending an email, creating a task, the moment a defined condition is met, a metric threshold breach, a Contact Lens finding, an evaluation completion, rather than a supervisor watching dashboards and reacting manually.
aws_connect_security_profile: `aws_connect_security_profile` defines a real set of permissions, which parts of the Connect instance and which actions, that gets attached to an `aws_connect_user`, the actual access-control mechanism behind what an agent, supervisor, or administrator can see and do.
aws_connect_task_template: `aws_connect_task_template` defines the real fields an agent fills in to create or complete a task, a follow-up, a case, a callback, so every task of that type captures the same structured information instead of an agent typing free-form notes.
aws_connect_test_case: `aws_connect_test_case` defines a real, simulated voice or chat interaction, the starting contact flow, phone number, caller intent, and expected response, that Connect's own native testing and simulation capability runs and scores pass or fail, validating a contact flow change before it reaches real customers.
aws_connect_traffic_distribution_group: `aws_connect_traffic_distribution_group` links `aws_connect_instance`s in different AWS Regions and distributes real inbound traffic to phone numbers attached to the group between them, the mechanism behind multi-Region resiliency and disaster recovery for a contact center.
aws_connect_user: `aws_connect_user` creates a real, individual agent, supervisor, or administrator account inside an `aws_connect_instance`, with an attached `aws_connect_security_profile` and `aws_connect_routing_profile` determining what they can do and what contacts they receive.
aws_connect_user_hierarchy_group: `aws_connect_user_hierarchy_group` organizes `aws_connect_user`s into a real, nested reporting structure, teams, regions, business units, used for filtered reporting and access scoping beyond what an `aws_connect_security_profile` alone controls.
aws_connect_view: `aws_connect_view` defines a real, custom UI template, built with HTML or JSX, that an `aws_connect_contact_flow`'s Show View block displays inside the agent workspace, guiding an agent through a task with a purpose-built screen instead of a generic one.
aws_connect_workspace: `aws_connect_workspace` is the real, single web application agents use day to day, the Contact Control Panel, step-by-step guides, customer profiles, cases, and AI assistance combined, rather than agents switching between several separate tools.
aws_control_tower_enabled_baseline: `aws_control_tower_enabled_baseline` applies a real, predefined baseline, a coherent set of resources and configuration for a specific governance purpose, to a target organizational unit in an `aws_control_tower_landing_zone`, Control Tower's newer, more granular alternative to enrolling an entire account through Account Factory.
aws_control_tower_enabled_control: `aws_control_tower_enabled_control` turns on a real, high-level governance rule, preventive, detective, or proactive, against an organizational unit or account in an `aws_control_tower_landing_zone`, the actual mechanism that keeps an environment from drifting away from its intended security and compliance baseline.
aws_control_tower_landing_zone: `aws_control_tower_landing_zone` is the real, enterprise-wide multi-account environment AWS Control Tower orchestrates on a caller's behalf, built on AWS Organizations, Service Catalog, and IAM Identity Center, the container every organizational unit, account, and control a Control Tower deployment governs lives inside.
aws_cur_report_definition: `aws_cur_report_definition` defines a real, recurring AWS Cost and Usage Report, its name, time granularity, file format, compression, and destination S3 bucket, that AWS delivers at least once a day so a caller has line-item-level billing data to analyze rather than only aggregate cost summaries.
aws_customer_gateway: `aws_customer_gateway` tells AWS the real, public-facing details, IP address among them, of an on-premises VPN device, the AWS-side resource a Site-to-Site VPN connection's two tunnels terminate against. It does not configure the physical or software device itself, a caller sets that up independently to match.
aws_customer_profiles_calculated_attribu: `aws_customer_profiles_calculated_attribute_definition` turns raw, real customer profile data into an actionable, derived metric, lifetime spend, days since last contact, inside an `aws_customer_profiles_domain`, used by segments and other Customer Profiles features rather than every consumer recomputing it independently.
aws_customer_profiles_domain: `aws_customer_profiles_domain` is where Amazon Connect Customer Profiles' real, unified customer data actually lives, the top-level container every `aws_customer_profiles_object_type`, integration, and profile inside one Customer Profiles deployment belongs to.
aws_customer_profiles_domain_object_type: `aws_customer_profiles_domain_object_type` is the real, domain-specific configuration of an `aws_customer_profiles_object_type`, applying that object type's schema within one particular `aws_customer_profiles_domain` rather than the type definition existing only in the abstract.
aws_customer_profiles_event_stream: `aws_customer_profiles_event_stream` streams real profile change events out of an `aws_customer_profiles_domain` as they happen, the mechanism for reacting to profile updates elsewhere rather than polling Customer Profiles for changes.
aws_customer_profiles_event_trigger: `aws_customer_profiles_event_trigger` reacts to a real incoming event on an `aws_customer_profiles_event_stream`, updating a segment or firing a downstream action, so a profile-affecting event is acted on as it arrives rather than only discoverable later on a schedule.
aws_customer_profiles_integration: `aws_customer_profiles_integration` connects an `aws_customer_profiles_domain` to a real external system, Salesforce, ServiceNow, an ERP, through a pre-built AppFlow connector, so third-party customer data merges automatically into Connect's own contact history rather than being manually imported.
aws_customer_profiles_object_type: `aws_customer_profiles_object_type` defines the real schema for one category of customer data, a purchase, a support ticket, that an `aws_customer_profiles_integration` ingests and Customer Profiles merges into a unified profile.
aws_customer_profiles_recommender: `aws_customer_profiles_recommender` generates real, personalized recommendations from an `aws_customer_profiles_domain`'s own unified profile data, surfaced back through the Customer Profiles API rather than a caller building a separate recommendation pipeline against the same data.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition: `aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition` groups real customer profiles sharing defined attributes, including calculated ones, into a segment that's dynamically re-evaluated as underlying attribute values change, rather than a static, one-time export of matching profiles.
aws_data_brew_dataset: `aws_data_brew_dataset` connects AWS Glue DataBrew to a real source of raw data, an S3 location among the supported sources, the actual input an `aws_data_brew_project` explores and an `aws_data_brew_job` transforms.
aws_data_brew_job: `aws_data_brew_job` actually runs an `aws_data_brew_recipe` against an `aws_data_brew_dataset` at production scale, terabytes of data, no infrastructure to provision, writing the cleaned, transformed output to S3.
aws_data_brew_project: `aws_data_brew_project` is DataBrew's real, interactive workspace, a grid view of an `aws_data_brew_dataset` where a caller explores value distributions and builds up an `aws_data_brew_recipe` of point-and-click transformations without writing code.
aws_data_brew_recipe: `aws_data_brew_recipe` is the real, saved sequence of transformations, chosen from DataBrew's 250-plus built-in options, built inside an `aws_data_brew_project` and then reusable, unchanged or updated, against other datasets rather than rebuilt from scratch each time.
aws_data_brew_ruleset: `aws_data_brew_ruleset` defines real data-quality rules, checks for nulls, valid ranges, expected formats, that get validated against an `aws_data_brew_dataset`, catching bad data before it flows further downstream rather than only after a job has already run.
aws_data_brew_schedule: `aws_data_brew_schedule` runs an `aws_data_brew_job` automatically on a real, recurring cadence, so a dataset stays continuously cleaned and transformed rather than requiring a caller to trigger every run by hand.
aws_data_exchange_data_set: `aws_data_exchange_data_set` is the real, curated resource a data provider assembles in AWS Data Exchange, files, an API, Redshift, S3, or Lake Formation data, that a receiver gains access to once they accept a real data grant or subscribe to a Marketplace data product built around it.
aws_data_exchange_event_action: `aws_data_exchange_event_action` automatically runs a real action, exporting to S3, for instance, whenever a specific event happens to an `aws_data_exchange_data_set`, a new revision being published, rather than a provider or receiver watching for that event and acting manually.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline: `aws_data_pipeline_pipeline` defines a scheduled, real data-movement and transformation workflow between AWS storage and compute services. AWS Data Pipeline stopped onboarding new customers on July 25, 2024; existing customers can continue using it, with AWS recommending AWS Glue, AWS Step Functions, or Amazon MWAA for new data-integration work.
aws_data_sync_location_azure_blob: `aws_data_sync_location_azure_blob` registers a real Microsoft Azure Blob Storage container as a DataSync transfer endpoint, one of several non-AWS cloud storage systems, alongside Google Cloud Storage and others, DataSync can transfer to or from directly.
aws_data_sync_location_efs: `aws_data_sync_location_efs` registers a real Amazon EFS file system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, the same real endpoint role as `aws_data_sync_location_s3` but for EFS instead of S3.
aws_data_sync_location_fsx_lustre: `aws_data_sync_location_fsx_lustre` registers a real Amazon FSx for Lustre file system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, used for high-performance computing and machine learning workloads that need Lustre's own throughput.
aws_data_sync_location_fsx_ontap: `aws_data_sync_location_fsx_ontap` registers a real Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, for migrating or replicating data to or from an existing NetApp-based storage environment.
aws_data_sync_location_fsx_open_zfs: `aws_data_sync_location_fsx_open_zfs` registers a real Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, the OpenZFS-compatible counterpart among DataSync's several managed FSx location types.
aws_data_sync_location_fsx_windows: `aws_data_sync_location_fsx_windows` registers a real Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, the managed Windows-file-server counterpart to `aws_data_sync_location_smb`.
aws_data_sync_location_hdfs: `aws_data_sync_location_hdfs` registers a real Hadoop Distributed File System cluster as a DataSync transfer endpoint, letting an `aws_data_sync_task` move data out of an on-premises big-data cluster into AWS storage.
aws_data_sync_location_nfs: `aws_data_sync_location_nfs` registers a real, on-premises NFS file share as a DataSync transfer endpoint, letting an `aws_data_sync_task` migrate or replicate data to or from on-premises storage rather than only between AWS services.
aws_data_sync_location_object_storage: `aws_data_sync_location_object_storage` registers a real, self-managed or third-party S3-compatible object storage system as a DataSync transfer endpoint, distinct from the AWS-managed `aws_data_sync_location_s3`.
aws_data_sync_location_s3: `aws_data_sync_location_s3` registers a real Amazon S3 bucket and prefix as a DataSync transfer endpoint, usable as either the source or destination of an `aws_data_sync_task`.
aws_data_sync_location_smb: `aws_data_sync_location_smb` registers a real, on-premises SMB file share as a DataSync transfer endpoint, the Windows-share counterpart to `aws_data_sync_location_nfs`.
aws_data_sync_task: `aws_data_sync_task` is the real, actual transfer definition in AWS DataSync, pairing a source `aws_data_sync_location_s3` (or another location type) with a destination location and running the encrypted, integrity-validated copy between them.
aws_data_zone_connection: `aws_data_zone_connection` is DataZone's newer, unified way of linking an `aws_data_zone_environment` to a real external data source or analytics tool, consolidating what earlier required several separate configuration steps into one reusable connection resource.
aws_data_zone_data_source: `aws_data_zone_data_source` publishes real data assets, from the AWS Glue Data Catalog or Amazon Redshift, into an `aws_data_zone_domain`'s own catalog, the actual mechanism by which raw AWS data becomes discoverable and requestable inside DataZone.
aws_data_zone_domain: `aws_data_zone_domain` is Amazon DataZone's top-level real container for cataloging, governing, and sharing data, the resource every `aws_data_zone_project`, `aws_data_zone_environment`, and business glossary in one DataZone deployment belongs to.
aws_data_zone_environment: `aws_data_zone_environment` deploys the real, underlying AWS resources, a Redshift cluster, a Glue database, that an `aws_data_zone_project`'s members actually query and analyze data through, provisioned from an `aws_data_zone_environment_profile` rather than set up by hand.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf: `aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_configuration` sets domain-wide defaults, IAM roles, regions, for how an `aws_data_zone_environment_profile` and the environments built from it are actually allowed to be provisioned within an `aws_data_zone_domain`.
aws_data_zone_environment_profile: `aws_data_zone_environment_profile` is a real, reusable configuration template an `aws_data_zone_environment` gets provisioned from, so every project's environment of a given kind is set up consistently rather than configured from scratch each time.
aws_data_zone_form_type: `aws_data_zone_form_type` defines a real, structured metadata schema, business glossary terms, custom attributes, attached to assets cataloged inside an `aws_data_zone_domain`, so catalog entries carry consistent, richer context than a bare technical schema alone.
aws_data_zone_owner: `aws_data_zone_owner` assigns real ownership of a domain unit or `aws_data_zone_project` to a specific user or group inside an `aws_data_zone_domain`, the accountable party DataZone's governance workflows route approvals and questions to.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant: `aws_data_zone_policy_grant` is the real, actual authorization grant that lets a specific principal perform an action, publishing an asset, creating an environment, within an `aws_data_zone_domain`, the enforcement mechanism behind DataZone's fine-grained governance model.
aws_data_zone_project: `aws_data_zone_project` is a real, collaborative workspace inside an `aws_data_zone_domain` where data workers, engineers, analysts, data scientists, actually discover, request access to, and work with cataloged data together.
aws_data_zone_project_membership: `aws_data_zone_project_membership` is the real, actual grant that adds a user or group to an `aws_data_zone_project`, distinct from an `aws_data_zone_owner` in that membership alone doesn't carry ownership-level accountability.
aws_data_zone_project_profile: `aws_data_zone_project_profile` is a real, reusable template an `aws_data_zone_project` can be created from within a domain, standardizing what resources and environments a new project of a given kind starts with rather than every project being configured individually from a blank slate.
aws_data_zone_subscription_target: `aws_data_zone_subscription_target` is the real, actual destination, a specific Redshift database or S3 location, that data gets delivered to once an `aws_data_zone_project` member's subscription request to an `aws_data_zone_data_source`'s asset is approved.
aws_data_zone_user_profile: `aws_data_zone_user_profile` represents one real, individual user's own identity and settings inside an `aws_data_zone_domain`, distinct from `aws_data_zone_project_membership`, which is that user's specific access to one project.
aws_dax_cluster: `aws_dax_cluster` creates a real, in-memory caching cluster in front of DynamoDB, Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator, that can cut microsecond-latency DynamoDB reads down to microseconds further still, transparent to the application beyond pointing its SDK client at the DAX cluster's own endpoint instead of DynamoDB directly.
aws_dax_parameter_group: `aws_dax_parameter_group` sets real, engine-level configuration, TTL and record count limits among them, for an `aws_dax_cluster`, kept as its own resource so the same parameter set can be applied consistently across multiple clusters.
aws_dax_subnet_group: `aws_dax_subnet_group` defines the real VPC subnets an `aws_dax_cluster`'s nodes are actually placed into, the network-placement configuration a cluster requires before it can be created.
aws_deadline_budget: `aws_deadline_budget` sets a real spending threshold for rendering activity within an `aws_deadline_farm`, tracked through Deadline Cloud's own cost management and usage explorer, so runaway render costs get flagged before a bill arrives rather than after.
aws_deadline_farm: `aws_deadline_farm` is AWS Deadline Cloud's real, top-level container, every `aws_deadline_queue`, `aws_deadline_fleet`, and job for one render or simulation workload belongs to exactly one farm, kept separate from other farms for isolating production from test environments.
aws_deadline_fleet: `aws_deadline_fleet` is a real, managed or customer-managed group of worker hosts that actually process jobs from an `aws_deadline_queue`, the core compute infrastructure behind an `aws_deadline_farm`, a single fleet able to serve multiple queues and a single queue able to draw from multiple fleets.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint: `aws_deadline_license_endpoint` provisions the real, VPC-hosted endpoint Deadline Cloud's usage-based licensing connects through, letting customer-managed fleets check out real, metered third-party software licenses for a job's duration rather than requiring a permanent per-seat license.
aws_deadline_limit: `aws_deadline_limit` caps real, concurrent consumption of a constrained resource, a software license seat, a database connection, across every job in an `aws_deadline_farm` that needs it, so jobs are scheduled only when the actual limited resource is available rather than starting and then failing partway through.
aws_deadline_metered_product: `aws_deadline_metered_product` is one real, usage-based-licensed software product made available through an `aws_deadline_license_endpoint`, added so an `aws_deadline_fleet`'s workers can check that specific product's license out for a job.
aws_deadline_monitor: `aws_deadline_monitor` is the real, separate web application Deadline Cloud provides for creating, managing, and monitoring farms, fleets, jobs, and users, distinct from the underlying `aws_deadline_farm` and its resources, which can also be managed entirely through the API or CLI without it.
aws_deadline_queue: `aws_deadline_queue` holds real jobs for scheduling onto an associated `aws_deadline_fleet`, and is Deadline Cloud's own primary permissions boundary, controlling who can see and submit to a given slice of an `aws_deadline_farm` rather than the farm as a whole.
aws_deadline_queue_environment: `aws_deadline_queue_environment` defines real setup and teardown scripts that run on a worker before and after a job from an `aws_deadline_queue`, license checkout, temp file cleanup, rather than every job needing to handle that itself.
aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association: `aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association` is the real, actual link between an `aws_deadline_queue` and an `aws_deadline_fleet`. A queue with no fleet association has nowhere to actually schedule its jobs to run.
aws_deadline_queue_limit_association: `aws_deadline_queue_limit_association` is the real, actual link between an `aws_deadline_queue` and an `aws_deadline_limit`. A limit defined but never associated with a queue never actually constrains any job.
aws_deadline_storage_profile: `aws_deadline_storage_profile` describes the real operating system and file-system layout of one workstation or worker configuration, letting Deadline Cloud derive path-mapping rules and transform file paths automatically when a job submitted from one storage profile runs on a worker with a different one.
aws_deadline_worker: `aws_deadline_worker` is a real, individual compute host, running the Deadline Cloud Worker Agent, that actually picks up and executes tasks from an `aws_deadline_queue` through its `aws_deadline_fleet`, reporting status and performance metrics back to the service as it works.
aws_detective_graph: `aws_detective_graph` is Amazon Detective's real behavior graph, built continuously from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty, and Security Hub findings across one or more linked accounts, correlating entities and their relationships over time so a security investigation can trace what happened rather than searching raw logs by hand.
aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space: `aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space` is a real, logical container defining the AWS account access, third-party integrations, and user permissions that AWS DevOps Agent, AWS's always-available operations teammate for incident response and reliability, is scoped to. AWS DevOps Agent launched in preview in December 2025 and became generally available in March 2026, genuinely new enough that its own resources are worth verifying live rather than assumed.
aws_dev_ops_guru_notification_channel: `aws_dev_ops_guru_notification_channel` sends a real SNS notification, filterable by severity, the moment DevOps Guru creates a new insight, up to two topics configurable so the right people or systems find out about a detected operational anomaly without polling the console.
aws_dev_ops_guru_resource_collection: `aws_dev_ops_guru_resource_collection` scopes which real AWS resources, identified by CloudFormation stack or by tag, DevOps Guru actually analyzes CloudWatch metrics and CloudTrail events for, so anomaly detection covers the resources that matter rather than every resource in the account indiscriminately.
aws_direct_connect_connection: `aws_direct_connect_connection` is the real, physical dedicated network connection between a caller's own network and an AWS Direct Connect location, the foundational resource every `aws_direct_connect_lag` and virtual interface ultimately runs over.
aws_direct_connect_direct_connect_gatewa: `aws_direct_connect_direct_connect_gateway` is a real, global resource that lets a single Direct Connect connection reach multiple VPCs across different AWS accounts and Regions, aggregating what would otherwise need a separate connection or virtual interface per VPC.
aws_direct_connect_lag: `aws_direct_connect_lag` bundles multiple `aws_direct_connect_connection`s into a single, real logical interface with combined bandwidth and automatic failover, the Direct Connect equivalent of link aggregation on a physical switch.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter: `aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_interface` carries real, private traffic over an `aws_direct_connect_connection` directly into a specific VPC, using a private, not public, ASN and IP addressing on the AWS side.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf: `aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interface` carries real traffic over an `aws_direct_connect_connection` to AWS's own public-facing services, S3, DynamoDB, and similar, over their public IP ranges, distinct from `aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_interface`'s route into a specific VPC.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter: `aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_interface` carries real traffic over an `aws_direct_connect_connection` into an EC2 Transit Gateway rather than directly into one VPC, letting a single Direct Connect connection reach every VPC attached to that transit gateway.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad: `aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad` provisions AWS Managed Microsoft AD, a real, actual Windows Server Active Directory running on AWS with Group Policy, trusts, schema extensions, and Kerberos authentication, rather than an AD-compatible but limited-feature substitute.
aws_directory_service_simple_ad: `aws_directory_service_simple_ad` provisions Simple AD, a Samba-based, lower-cost, feature-limited directory compared to `aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad`, suited to workloads needing basic AD compatibility rather than full Microsoft AD fidelity. Simple AD closed to new customers on July 30, 2026; existing directories and integrated workloads continue functioning, with AWS pointing new customers to AWS Managed Microsoft AD or AD Connector instead.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy: `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` automates the real, recurring creation, retention, and deletion of EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs on a defined schedule, so backups happen consistently without a caller manually creating or cleaning up snapshots.
aws_dms_data_migration: `aws_dms_data_migration` is the real, actual DMS Serverless data migration run from within an `aws_dms_migration_project`, moving data between the source and target already defined by that project's own data providers.
aws_dms_data_provider: `aws_dms_data_provider` defines the connection details for one real, self-managed or fully managed database engine, usable inside an `aws_dms_migration_project` for AWS DMS Schema Conversion, distinct from an `aws_dms_endpoint`, which serves an actual running `aws_dms_replication_task` instead.
aws_dms_endpoint: `aws_dms_endpoint` defines the real connection details, engine type, credentials, and location, for one source or target database that an `aws_dms_replication_task` or `aws_dms_replication_config` actually migrates data to or from.
aws_dms_event_subscription: `aws_dms_event_subscription` sends a real SNS notification when a specific event happens to an `aws_dms_replication_instance` or `aws_dms_replication_task`, a failure, a state change, rather than a caller polling DMS to notice.
aws_dms_migration_project: `aws_dms_migration_project` ties together source and target `aws_dms_data_provider`s, an instance profile, and transformation rules for AWS DMS Schema Conversion, the real project a caller uses to assess and convert database schemas to a new target engine before migrating the actual data.
aws_dms_replication_config: `aws_dms_replication_config` defines a real, serverless replication, DMS automatically provisions, scales, and manages the underlying compute rather than a caller sizing and managing an `aws_dms_replication_instance` by hand.
aws_dms_replication_instance: `aws_dms_replication_instance` is the real, managed compute that actually runs an `aws_dms_replication_task`'s migration or ongoing change-data-capture work between its source and target `aws_dms_endpoint`s.
aws_dms_replication_subnet_group: `aws_dms_replication_subnet_group` defines the real VPC subnets an `aws_dms_replication_instance` is actually placed into, network placement a replication instance requires before it can be created.
aws_dms_replication_task: `aws_dms_replication_task` is the real, actual migration or CDC job that runs on an `aws_dms_replication_instance`, moving data from a source `aws_dms_endpoint` to a target one.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster: `aws_doc_db_dbcluster` creates a real Amazon DocumentDB cluster, MongoDB-API-compatible, with storage automatically replicated across Availability Zones, the container every `aws_doc_db_dbinstance` in a cluster-based deployment belongs to.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group: `aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group` sets real, engine-level configuration for an `aws_doc_db_dbcluster`, kept as its own resource so the same parameter set can be applied consistently across multiple clusters.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance: `aws_doc_db_dbinstance` adds real compute capacity to an `aws_doc_db_dbcluster`, the actual instance that serves reads and, for the primary instance, writes against the cluster's own shared storage.
aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group: `aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group` defines the real VPC subnets an `aws_doc_db_dbcluster`'s instances are actually placed into, required network placement before a cluster can be created.
aws_doc_db_global_cluster: `aws_doc_db_global_cluster` links `aws_doc_db_dbcluster`s across multiple AWS Regions with fast, storage-based replication, real cross-Region disaster recovery and low-latency global reads that a single-Region cluster can't provide on its own.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster: `aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster` creates a real, hash-sharded DocumentDB deployment that scales to millions of reads and writes per second and petabytes of storage without the caller choosing, managing, or upgrading individual instances the way an `aws_doc_db_dbcluster` requires.
aws_drs_source_network: `aws_drs_source_network` replicates a real, in-AWS network's own configuration, subnet CIDRs, security groups, route tables, internet gateways, into AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, so a recovery launch reproduces the source network's actual layout instead of requiring it to be rebuilt from scratch during a failover.
aws_dsql_cluster: `aws_dsql_cluster` creates a real Aurora DSQL cluster, a serverless, PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL database with independently scaling compute, commit, and storage components and no single leader, built for 99.99% single-Region or 99.999% multi-Region availability without a caller sharding or upgrading instances.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table: `aws_dynamo_db_global_table` replicates an `aws_dynamo_db_table`'s own data across multiple AWS Regions with active-active, multi-Region writes, real low-latency global access and Regional failover that a single-Region table doesn't provide.
aws_dynamo_db_table: `aws_dynamo_db_table` creates a real, single-Region DynamoDB table, AWS's managed key-value and document database, with automatically scaling throughput and no servers for a caller to provision or patch.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation: `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` reserves real EC2 capacity for a specific instance type and Availability Zone, guaranteeing it's available when needed regardless of what else is running in that zone, independent of any particular Reserved Instance or Savings Plan billing commitment.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet: `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet` groups several `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation`s across instance types into one, real fleet-level target capacity, so a caller reserves a total amount of compute rather than managing each individual reservation by hand.
aws_ec2_carrier_gateway: `aws_ec2_carrier_gateway` connects a VPC in an AWS Wavelength Zone to a real telecommunications carrier's own network, letting traffic route to and from mobile devices on that carrier's 4G/5G network with the low latency Wavelength is built for.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule: `aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule` grants a real, specific group of connected users access to a defined network CIDR through an `aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint`, without it, a connected client reaches nothing regardless of network association.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint: `aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint` provisions a real, managed OpenVPN-based endpoint that individual users connect to over a client VPN application, terminating their connection and routing them into an associated VPC, distinct from `aws_customer_gateway`'s site-to-site model connecting whole networks together.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_route: `aws_ec2_client_vpn_route` adds a real, specific route to an `aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint`'s own route table, directing connected clients' traffic for a given destination, beyond the routes that get created automatically from its network associations.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ: `aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_association` is the real, actual link between an `aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint` and a specific VPC subnet. An endpoint with no target network association has nowhere to actually route connected clients' traffic.
aws_ec2_dhcpoptions: `aws_ec2_dhcpoptions` defines the real DNS servers, domain name, and NTP servers that EC2 instances in an associated VPC receive automatically through DHCP, rather than every instance requiring manual network configuration.
aws_ec2_eipassociation: `aws_ec2_eipassociation` is the real, actual grant that attaches an existing Elastic IP address to a specific EC2 instance or network interface. An allocated Elastic IP with no association isn't routing any traffic to anything yet.
aws_ec2_fleet: `aws_ec2_fleet` launches a real, defined mix of On-Demand, Spot, and Reserved Instance capacity across multiple instance types and Availability Zones from one request, rather than a caller managing separate launch requests per purchasing option.
aws_ec2_host: `aws_ec2_host` allocates a real, physical EC2 server, a Dedicated Host, dedicated entirely to a caller's own use, needed for software that's licensed per physical core or socket, or for regulatory requirements around instance isolation that shared hardware doesn't satisfy.
aws_ec2_instance_connect_endpoint: `aws_ec2_instance_connect_endpoint` lets a caller SSH or RDP into a real EC2 instance in a private subnet, no public IP, no bastion host, no VPN, needed, connecting through the endpoint from the console or CLI instead.
aws_ec2_ipam: `aws_ec2_ipam` is the real, top-level IP Address Manager resource, planning, tracking, and monitoring IP address usage across an AWS organization's accounts and Regions from one place rather than each account managing its own address space independently.
aws_ec2_ipamallocation: `aws_ec2_ipamallocation` is a real, specific CIDR reservation carved out of an `aws_ec2_ipampool`, tracked so IPAM knows that range is spoken for even before a real resource like a VPC is actually created to use it.
aws_ec2_ipampool: `aws_ec2_ipampool` is a real, defined group of CIDR ranges within an `aws_ec2_ipam` scope that VPCs and subnets actually allocate their own address space from, rather than a caller assigning CIDRs by hand and risking an overlap.
aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver: `aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver` automatically selects real CIDRs out of an `aws_ec2_ipam`'s own advanced-tier address database based on defined matching rules, and keeps a customer-managed prefix list synchronized with the result, so a prefix list used in a security group or route table stays current with IPAM's own data instead of being updated by hand.
aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver_target: `aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver_target` is the real, actual association between a specific customer-managed prefix list and an `aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver`, the resolver's selected CIDRs have nowhere to actually be synchronized to without one.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery: `aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery` finds and tracks real, existing IP-address-consuming resources, VPCs, subnets, Elastic IPs, across an organization's accounts for an `aws_ec2_ipam` to actually monitor, including resources IPAM didn't itself allocate the address space for.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery_associati: `aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery_association` is the real, actual link between an `aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery` and the specific `aws_ec2_ipam` it feeds discovered resource data into, needed since a resource discovery can in principle serve more than one IPAM.
aws_ec2_ipamscope: `aws_ec2_ipamscope` partitions an `aws_ec2_ipam`'s address space into a real, distinct pool of CIDRs, public, private, or a caller-defined custom scope, kept separate so address planning for internet-routable and private ranges don't overlap or interfere.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table: `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table` defines real routing for an AWS Outposts local gateway, controlling how traffic moves between the Outpost's own local network and the VPC it's associated with.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtua: `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtual_interface_group_association` is the real, actual link between an `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table` and an `aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface_group`, determining which physical interfaces that route table's routes apply across.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcass: `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcassociation` is the real, actual link between an `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table` and a specific VPC, determining which VPC's traffic that local gateway route table actually governs.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface: `aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface` is one real, physical network interface on an AWS Outposts local gateway, the actual link-layer connection an `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table` routes traffic across.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface_: `aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface_group` bundles multiple `aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface`s together, the real grouping an `aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtual_interface_group_association` actually references rather than each interface being wired to a route table individually.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry: `aws_ec2_network_acl_entry` defines one real, numbered, stateless allow or deny rule inside a network ACL, evaluated in rule-number order, the actual, individually addressable rule resource within a network ACL's broader rule set.
aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope: `aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope` defines a real, broader set of network paths and conditions to evaluate together, going beyond one `aws_ec2_network_insights_path`'s single source-destination pair to check an entire access boundary, everything that should or shouldn't be reachable from the internet, for instance, at once.
aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope_an: `aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope_analysis` runs a real, point-in-time check of an `aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope`, the access-scope counterpart to what an `aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis` does for a single `aws_ec2_network_insights_path`.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis: `aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis` runs a real, point-in-time check of an `aws_ec2_network_insights_path`, tracing every hop, security group, route table, network ACL, and reporting exactly where connectivity actually breaks if it does.
aws_ec2_network_insights_path: `aws_ec2_network_insights_path` defines a real source and destination for VPC Reachability Analyzer to trace, the actual path definition an `aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis` runs its point-in-time check against.
aws_ec2_prefix_list: `aws_ec2_prefix_list` is a real, named, reusable set of CIDR blocks a caller manages once and references from security group rules and route tables, so updating the underlying IP ranges doesn't mean editing every rule that uses them individually.
aws_ec2_route_server_endpoint: `aws_ec2_route_server_endpoint` is a real BGP peering point for VPC Route Server, AWS-managed BGP infrastructure that speaks with third-party routing appliances inside a VPC and dynamically updates the VPC's own route tables, an alternative to static routing for workloads that need dynamic, fault-tolerant routing entirely inside a VPC.
aws_ec2_security_group_egress: `aws_ec2_security_group_egress` defines one real, specific outbound traffic rule on a security group, the actual, individually addressable rule resource, as distinct from managing a security group's entire rule set as one inline block.
aws_ec2_security_group_vpc_association: `aws_ec2_security_group_vpc_association` shares an existing security group across additional VPCs in the same Region, a real, direct alternative to recreating the same rule set in every VPC that needs it.
aws_ec2_spot_fleet: `aws_ec2_spot_fleet` launches and maintains a real target amount of Spot Instance capacity across multiple instance types and Availability Zones, automatically requesting replacement capacity if Spot Instances are interrupted, the Spot-focused predecessor to the more general `aws_ec2_fleet`.
aws_ec2_subnet_network_acl_association: `aws_ec2_subnet_network_acl_association` is the real, actual link between a subnet and the network ACL whose `aws_ec2_network_acl_entry` rules govern it, a subnet is always associated with exactly one network ACL, this association is what determines which one.
aws_ec2_subnet_route_table_association: `aws_ec2_subnet_route_table_association` is the real, actual link between a subnet and the route table whose routes govern traffic leaving it, a subnet uses its VPC's main route table unless a specific association like this one overrides it.
aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter: `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter` defines which real traffic, by protocol, port, and direction, actually gets copied out of a monitored network interface, the rules an `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_session` applies rather than mirroring every packet indiscriminately.
aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter_rule: `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter_rule` is one real, specific accept or reject rule inside an `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter`, the actual, individually addressable rule resource within a filter's broader rule set.
aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_session: `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_session` is the real, actual mirroring in progress, pairing a source network interface with an `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_filter` and an `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_target` the filtered traffic actually gets sent to.
aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_target: `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_target` is the real destination, a network interface, a Network Load Balancer, that an `aws_ec2_traffic_mirror_session`'s mirrored, filtered traffic actually gets delivered to for analysis by an intrusion-detection or packet-inspection tool.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway` is a real, central hub that VPCs, VPN connections, and Direct Connect gateways attach to, letting traffic route between all of them through one managed device instead of a full mesh of individual peering connections.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment` is the real, general resource connecting a VPC, VPN, Direct Connect gateway, or another transit gateway to an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, the actual link every specific attachment type shares the same underlying mechanism for.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_connect: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_connect` is a real, GRE-based attachment type on an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway` built for connecting third-party SD-WAN appliances, supporting higher bandwidth per attachment than a standard VPN attachment.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_connect_peer: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_connect_peer` establishes a real BGP peering session over an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_connect` attachment, the actual routing adjacency an SD-WAN appliance needs beyond the GRE tunnel itself.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_metering_policy_: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_metering_policy_entry` defines a real, ordered rule that attributes an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`'s own metered usage for matching traffic, by attachment type, CIDR, protocol, and port, to a specific AWS account, so cross-account cost allocation for shared transit gateway traffic reflects who actually used it rather than defaulting entirely to the transit gateway owner.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_multicast_domain: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_multicast_domain` enables real multicast traffic to be routed between VPC attachments on an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, a capability a transit gateway's own standard unicast routing doesn't provide.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_peering_attachme: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_peering_attachment` connects two `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`s together, in the same or different Regions, the real mechanism for extending transit gateway routing across Regions without every VPC needing its own cross-Region connection.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_policy_table: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_policy_table` routes traffic on an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway` by matching real packet attributes, not just destination CIDR the way an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table` does, policy-based routing for cases where source, protocol, or port need to influence the path.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_policy_table_ent: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_policy_table_entry` is one real, specific matching rule inside an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_policy_table`, the actual, individually addressable rule within a policy table's broader rule set.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table` controls real routing between the attachments on an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, which VPCs, VPNs, and other attachments can reach which others through it, rather than every attachment being able to reach every other one by default.
aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment: `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment` is the real, specific `aws_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment` type connecting a VPC to an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, the most common way traffic actually reaches a transit gateway from inside a VPC.
aws_ec2_verified_access_endpoint: `aws_ec2_verified_access_endpoint` is the real, actual application Verified Access provides access to, an IP address, load balancer, or network interface, evaluated against its `aws_ec2_verified_access_group`'s policy on every request before traffic is allowed through.
aws_ec2_verified_access_group: `aws_ec2_verified_access_group` collects `aws_ec2_verified_access_endpoint`s with real, similar security requirements under one shared Verified Access policy, so a caller manages one policy per group of applications instead of one per individual endpoint.
aws_ec2_verified_access_instance: `aws_ec2_verified_access_instance` is the real, top-level AWS Verified Access resource that `aws_ec2_verified_access_trust_provider`s attach to, evaluating every request against zero-trust policies instead of relying on a traditional VPN for private application access.
aws_ec2_verified_access_trust_provider: `aws_ec2_verified_access_trust_provider` supplies the real identity or device-posture signal, an OIDC identity provider or a device-management agent, that Verified Access evaluates a request against, the actual source of trust its policies are written in terms of.
aws_ec2_volume: `aws_ec2_volume` creates a real, persistent Amazon EBS block storage volume, attachable to an EC2 instance, that keeps its own data independently of any single instance's own lifecycle.
aws_ec2_vpcblock_public_access_exclusion: `aws_ec2_vpcblock_public_access_exclusion` exempts a specific real VPC or subnet from the account's own VPC Block Public Access mode, bidirectionally or egress-only, so that one exception doesn't disrupt traffic when block-public-access is turned on account-wide.
aws_ec2_vpcencryption_control: `aws_ec2_vpcencryption_control` monitors, or in enforce mode actually blocks, cleartext traffic within and across VPCs in a Region, real, centralized enforcement of encryption in transit. T3, T3a, and T4g instances don't support the encryption VPC Encryption Controls requires and can't be used in an enforced subnet. AWS began charging for this feature by the hour per enabled VPC starting March 1, 2026, after a free introductory period.
aws_ec2_vpcendpoint: `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint` lets a VPC reach an AWS service, or a real, specific `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service` another account exposes, privately, without traffic ever crossing the public internet, the caller side of what AWS PrivateLink actually connects to.
aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service: `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service` exposes a caller's own real application as a PrivateLink service that other accounts' `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint`s can connect to, the provider side of the same PrivateLink connection.
aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service_permissions: `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service_permissions` controls which real AWS principals are actually allowed to create an `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint` against an `aws_ec2_vpcendpoint_service`, an allowlist a service owner manages rather than leaving their PrivateLink service open to any account that discovers it.
aws_ec2_vpcpeering_connection: `aws_ec2_vpcpeering_connection` directly connects two VPCs' own private IP address spaces, letting instances in each communicate as if on the same network, without a transit gateway, a VPN, or traffic ever leaving AWS's own backbone.
aws_ec2_vpnconcentrator: `aws_ec2_vpnconcentrator` aggregates up to 100 real, low-bandwidth (under 100 Mbps each) Site-to-Site VPN connections through a single, BGP-only resource attached to an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, built for connecting a large number of small remote sites, retail locations, branch offices, rather than provisioning a separate `aws_ec2_vpnconnection` for each one. Launched November 2025.
aws_ec2_vpnconnection: `aws_ec2_vpnconnection` establishes a real, encrypted Site-to-Site VPN connection with two tunnels for high availability, between a caller's own `aws_customer_gateway` and either a virtual private gateway or an `aws_ec2_transit_gateway`.
aws_ec2_vpngateway: `aws_ec2_vpngateway` is the real, AWS-side endpoint, a virtual private gateway, that a `aws_ec2_vpnconnection`'s tunnels terminate against inside a VPC, the counterpart to an `aws_customer_gateway` on the caller's own side of a Site-to-Site VPN connection.
aws_ec2_vpngateway_route_propagation: `aws_ec2_vpngateway_route_propagation` automatically propagates real routes learned over an `aws_ec2_vpngateway`'s BGP session into a specific route table, so a caller doesn't have to add static routes by hand every time the VPN's own advertised routes change.
aws_ecr_public_repository: `aws_ecr_public_repository` creates a real, publicly readable repository in the Amazon ECR Public Gallery, distinct from `aws_ecr_repository`'s own private-by-default model, letting anyone pull an image without AWS credentials.
aws_ecr_registry_scanning_configuration: `aws_ecr_registry_scanning_configuration` sets real, registry-wide image vulnerability scanning rules, basic or enhanced, applied automatically across every `aws_ecr_repository` matching a defined filter, rather than a caller configuring scanning on each repository individually.
aws_ecr_replication_configuration: `aws_ecr_replication_configuration` automatically copies real images pushed to an `aws_ecr_repository` into other Regions or accounts, so a caller doesn't have to build and maintain their own image-copying pipeline for multi-Region availability.
aws_ecr_repository:
`aws_ecr_repository` creates a real, private ECR repository for storing
container images, with real, configurable scanning and mutability
settings.
aws_ecr_repository_creation_template: `aws_ecr_repository_creation_template` defines the real settings, access policy, tag immutability, encryption, lifecycle rules, applied automatically to repositories ECR creates on a caller's behalf during pull-through cache or replication, matched to a specific repository-name prefix rather than every auto-created repository defaulting to ECR's own bare settings.
aws_ecr_signing_configuration: `aws_ecr_signing_configuration` references one or more Signer signing profiles, and optionally repository filters, so ECR automatically signs an image with the identity of whoever pushed it the moment it's pushed, up to 10 signing rules per registry for stronger security boundaries, without a caller signing images manually as a separate step. Launched November 2025.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider: `aws_ecs_capacity_provider` defines a real source of compute, an Auto Scaling group or Fargate, that an `aws_ecs_cluster` can actually launch tasks onto, and the scaling behavior ECS should apply as task demand changes.
aws_ecs_cluster: `aws_ecs_cluster` is the real, logical grouping of tasks and services, backed by EC2 instances, Fargate, or both, that every `aws_ecs_service` and `aws_ecs_task_definition` run gets scheduled into.
aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_provider_associ: `aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_provider_associations` is the real, actual link between an `aws_ecs_cluster` and one or more `aws_ecs_capacity_provider`s, along with the cluster's own default capacity provider strategy.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition: `aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition` runs exactly one real task on every active EC2 container instance in an `aws_ecs_cluster` that meets its placement constraints, prioritized to launch first and stop last among that instance's tasks, ECS's own managed-daemon pattern for agents like security or observability tooling that every instance needs running.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service: `aws_ecs_express_gateway_service` deploys a production-ready, HTTPS-reachable containerized web application from just a container image and two IAM roles, ECS Express Mode automatically provisioning and configuring the Application Load Balancer, target group, security group, and auto-scaling policy a caller would otherwise assemble by hand, with an AWS-provided domain name available immediately. Announced November 2025 at re:Invent.
aws_ecs_service: `aws_ecs_service` keeps a real, defined number of an `aws_ecs_task_definition`'s tasks running continuously in an `aws_ecs_cluster`, replacing failed tasks automatically and optionally integrating with a load balancer, the mechanism behind a long-running application rather than a one-off batch task.
aws_ecs_task_definition: `aws_ecs_task_definition` is the real blueprint, container images, CPU and memory, networking mode, IAM roles, that an `aws_ecs_service` or a standalone task actually launches from.
aws_ecs_task_set: `aws_ecs_task_set` is a real, specific version of an `aws_ecs_service`'s own tasks and its deployment configuration, the actual mechanism behind blue/green deployments where two task sets run side by side before traffic shifts fully to the new one.
aws_efs_access_point: `aws_efs_access_point` is a real, application-specific entry point into an `aws_efs_file_system`, enforcing its own POSIX user identity and a fixed root directory, so different applications sharing the same file system see only their own scoped directory rather than the file system's full root.
aws_efs_file_system: `aws_efs_file_system` creates a real, elastic, fully managed NFS file system that scales automatically as files are added and removed, mountable concurrently from many EC2 instances or containers at once.
aws_efs_mount_target: `aws_efs_mount_target` is the real, actual network endpoint, one per Availability Zone, that an EC2 instance or container in a specific subnet mounts an `aws_efs_file_system` through. A file system with no mount target in a given AZ can't be reached from resources there.
aws_egress_only_internet_gateway: `aws_egress_only_internet_gateway` lets IPv6 resources in a VPC initiate outbound connections to the internet while blocking any inbound connection from initiating one back, the IPv6-only, egress-only counterpart to a NAT gateway, which IPv6 doesn't use.
aws_eip: `aws_eip` allocates a real, static public IPv4 (or IPv6) address to a caller's own AWS account, remaining reserved and reachable at the same address even as it's associated with, or moved between, different EC2 instances or network interfaces over time.
aws_eks_access_entry: `aws_eks_access_entry` grants a real IAM principal access to an `aws_eks_cluster`'s Kubernetes API, EKS's own current, native authentication and authorization mechanism that replaced the older aws-auth ConfigMap approach.
aws_eks_addon: `aws_eks_addon` installs and manages a real, EKS-curated operational component, the VPC CNI, CoreDNS, kube-proxy among common ones, on an `aws_eks_cluster`, with its own version tracking and update lifecycle handled by EKS rather than a caller applying manifests and managing upgrades by hand.
aws_eks_capability: `aws_eks_capability` installs a real, fully managed, opinionated Kubernetes-native platform feature, Argo CD for continuous deployment, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes for AWS resource management, Kube Resource Orchestrator, running entirely in AWS-managed infrastructure rather than consuming an `aws_eks_cluster`'s own compute. Reached general availability November 30, 2025.
aws_eks_cluster: `aws_eks_cluster` runs the real, managed Kubernetes control plane, API server, etcd, scheduler, that every `aws_eks_nodegroup` and Fargate profile in an EKS deployment runs its actual workloads against.
aws_eks_fargate_profile: `aws_eks_fargate_profile` matches real pods in an `aws_eks_cluster`, by namespace and label selector, to run on Fargate rather than an `aws_eks_nodegroup`'s own EC2 worker nodes, no node to provision or patch for the pods it covers.
aws_eks_identity_provider_config: `aws_eks_identity_provider_config` federates an `aws_eks_cluster`'s Kubernetes API with an external OIDC identity provider, letting a caller authenticate to the cluster with their own organization's existing identity system instead of only IAM.
aws_eks_nodegroup: `aws_eks_nodegroup` provisions and manages a real group of EC2 worker nodes, patched and scaled by EKS itself, that join an `aws_eks_cluster` to actually run pods, an alternative to Fargate for workloads that need EC2-level control.
aws_eks_pod_identity_association: `aws_eks_pod_identity_association` maps a real IAM role to a Kubernetes service account in an `aws_eks_cluster`, giving pods using that service account automatically rotated, temporary AWS credentials without the OIDC-provider setup IAM roles for service accounts requires.
aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster: `aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster` creates a real Memcached or single-node Redis OSS/Valkey cache cluster, ElastiCache's original, foundational deployment model, distinct from `aws_elasti_cache_replication_group`'s own multi-node, automatic-failover architecture.
aws_elasti_cache_global_replication_grou: `aws_elasti_cache_global_replication_group` links `aws_elasti_cache_replication_group`s across multiple AWS Regions with cross-Region replication, real disaster recovery and low-latency global reads that a single-Region replication group can't provide on its own.
aws_elasti_cache_parameter_group: `aws_elasti_cache_parameter_group` sets real, engine-level configuration for an `aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster` or `aws_elasti_cache_replication_group`, kept as its own resource so the same parameter set can be applied consistently across multiple clusters.
aws_elasti_cache_replication_group: `aws_elasti_cache_replication_group` creates a real Redis OSS or Valkey deployment with primary and replica nodes and automatic failover, ElastiCache's high-availability alternative to a single-node `aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster`.
aws_elasti_cache_security_group_ingress: `aws_elasti_cache_security_group_ingress` authorizes real network access to an `aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster` running in the legacy EC2-Classic network model, a mechanism specific to accounts still using EC2-Classic rather than a VPC.
aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache: `aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache` creates a real ElastiCache deployment, Redis OSS, Valkey, or Memcached, that scales storage and compute automatically with actual usage, no node type to pick and no capacity to provision ahead of time the way `aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster` and `aws_elasti_cache_replication_group` both require.
aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache_snapsh: `aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache_snapshot` is a real, point-in-time backup of an `aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache`, restorable to a new serverless cache, the serverless-cache counterpart to snapshotting a provisioned cluster.
