Changing a key's spec, usage, origin, or multi-Region setting on an existing key is blocked outright, a deliberate guard against silently destroying key material.
aws_kms_replica_key: `aws_kms_replica_key` creates a real multi-Region replica of an `aws_kms_key` primary key in a different AWS Region. A replica shares its primary's key ID, key material, key spec, key usage, and rotation status, so data encrypted under the key in one Region can be decrypted under the replica in another without a cross-Region call or exposing plaintext in transit.
aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings: `aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings` configures the real account-level defaults for AWS Lake Formation, including data lake administrators and whether new Data Catalog databases and tables default to Lake Formation's own permission model or fall back to legacy IAM-only access.
aws_lake_formation_permissions: `aws_lake_formation_permissions` grants a real Lake Formation permission to a principal on a Data Catalog resource (a database or table) using Lake Formation's original, resource-by-resource grant model, the predecessor to the newer `aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions`, which additionally supports LF-Tag-based grants at scale.
aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions: `aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions` grants a real Lake Formation permission to a principal on a Data Catalog resource, AWS's current, recommended permission model, which supports both direct resource grants and LF-Tag-based access control for managing permissions across large numbers of databases and tables at once.
aws_lake_formation_resource: `aws_lake_formation_resource` registers a real S3 location with Lake Formation, the real prerequisite step that brings that storage location under Lake Formation's own permission model rather than leaving access to bucket policies and IAM alone.
aws_lake_formation_tag: `aws_lake_formation_tag` defines a real LF-Tag, a key with one or more allowed values, such as `department` with values `sales`, `marketing`, `engineering`, used as the building block of Lake Formation's tag-based access control.
aws_lake_formation_tag_association: `aws_lake_formation_tag_association` attaches a real `aws_lake_formation_tag` to a Data Catalog resource or table column, so that principals granted matching tags, rather than an explicit per-resource grant, gain access to it.
aws_lambda_alias: `aws_lambda_alias` creates a real named, mutable pointer to a specific published version of an `aws_lambda_function`, so callers can be redirected to a new version, or gradually shifted to one with weighted traffic, without changing the ARN they invoke.
aws_lambda_code_signing_config: `aws_lambda_code_signing_config` defines a real policy that requires deployed Lambda function code to be signed by a trusted AWS Signer profile before Lambda will accept it, rejecting unsigned or tampered deployment packages.
aws_lambda_event_source_mapping: `aws_lambda_event_source_mapping` creates a real subscription that polls a stream or queue, a Kinesis stream, a DynamoDB stream, an SQS queue, an MSK or self-managed Kafka topic, and invokes an `aws_lambda_function` with the batched records it reads.
aws_lambda_function: `aws_lambda_function` creates a real Lambda function: its deployment package or container image, runtime, handler, memory, timeout, and execution role, the real unit of code AWS Lambda runs on demand.
aws_lambda_layer_version: `aws_lambda_layer_version` publishes a real immutable version of a Lambda layer, a zip archive of libraries or other dependencies that one or more `aws_lambda_function`s can include without bundling that content into each function's own deployment package.
aws_lambda_microvm_image: `aws_lambda_microvm_image` builds a real versioned image, a Dockerfile plus application artifacts uploaded to S3, that Lambda MicroVMs launch on demand as individually isolated, VM-level-sandboxed compute instances. This is a genuinely new AWS service: Lambda MicroVMs launched June 22, 2026, expanded from an initial five AWS Regions to ten as of August 2026, and is recent enough that not all of its behavior is covered by pre-2026 general knowledge.
aws_lambda_permission: `aws_lambda_permission` grants a real resource-based permission on an `aws_lambda_function` or its alias, allowing a specific AWS service or account to invoke it, the mechanism behind, for example, API Gateway or S3 being allowed to call a function directly.
aws_lambda_url: `aws_lambda_url` creates a real, dedicated HTTPS endpoint for an `aws_lambda_function`, letting the function be invoked directly over HTTP without provisioning API Gateway in front of it.
aws_launch_configuration: `aws_launch_configuration` defines a real, legacy Auto Scaling launch template predecessor: instance type, AMI, and instance-level settings for instances an Auto Scaling group launches. AWS deprecated launch configurations in favor of `aws_launch_template`: no new EC2 features have been added to launch configurations since January 2023, and as of October 1, 2024 new AWS accounts cannot create a launch configuration through any method, console, API, CLI, or CloudFormation. Existing launch configurations in older accounts continue to function.
aws_launch_template: `aws_launch_template` defines a real, versioned template of instance launch parameters, AMI, instance type, key pair, security groups, and more, that EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EC2 Fleet, and Spot Fleet all launch instances from. It is the current, actively developed successor to the deprecated `aws_launch_configuration`, adding version history and support for the latest EC2 features.
aws_launch_wizard_deployment: `aws_launch_wizard_deployment` deploys a real, sized and configured workload, third-party software such as SQL Server or SAP, or a supported AWS workload pattern, using AWS Launch Wizard's own guided, Well-Architected-aligned automation rather than a hand-built template.
aws_lex_bot: `aws_lex_bot` creates a real Amazon Lex V2 conversational bot: its locales, intents, and IAM role. Lex V2 is the only Lex generation CloudFormation supports; the original Lex V1 has no CloudFormation resource type of its own.
aws_lex_bot_alias: `aws_lex_bot_alias` creates a real named pointer to a specific `aws_lex_bot_version`, letting a calling application be redirected to a new bot version, for example promoting a tested version to a `PROD` alias, without changing the identifier the application calls.
aws_lex_bot_version: `aws_lex_bot_version` publishes a real, immutable numbered snapshot of an `aws_lex_bot`'s current DRAFT configuration. If the DRAFT is unchanged since the last version was created, Amazon Lex returns that existing version rather than creating a duplicate.
aws_license_manager_grant: `aws_license_manager_grant` shares a real `aws_license_manager_license`'s entitlements with a specific AWS account, organizational unit, or organization, the mechanism a license owner uses to let another account consume a license it granted from AWS Marketplace or a direct seller integration.
aws_license_manager_license: `aws_license_manager_license` represents a real granted license for a product purchased from AWS Marketplace or from a seller integrated with AWS License Manager's managed entitlements, tracking the license's entitlements, validity period, and consumption rules.
aws_license_manager_license_asset_rule_s: `aws_license_manager_license_asset_rule_set` defines a real named set of rules that govern how an `aws_license_manager_license`'s usage is tracked and enforced against the physical or virtual assets consuming it. This resource type has only thin official documentation, an API reference entry rather than a full guide, verified live this session rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_lightsail_alarm: `aws_lightsail_alarm` creates a real CloudWatch-backed alarm scoped to a single Lightsail resource, an instance, database, distribution, or load balancer, notifying when one of that resource's own metrics crosses a threshold.
aws_lightsail_bucket: `aws_lightsail_bucket` creates a real Lightsail object storage bucket, built on S3, for storing files at Lightsail's simplified, predictable-pricing tier rather than through the full S3 console.
aws_lightsail_certificate: `aws_lightsail_certificate` provisions a real SSL/TLS certificate for use with Lightsail resources, such as a content delivery distribution, validated and issued the way an ACM certificate is but managed within Lightsail's own simplified surface.
aws_lightsail_container: `aws_lightsail_container` creates a real Lightsail Container Service, a managed environment that deploys and runs containerized applications, images pushed via Docker, without the operational surface of a full ECS or EKS cluster.
aws_lightsail_database: `aws_lightsail_database` creates a real managed relational database, MySQL or PostgreSQL, at Lightsail's simplified, flat-rate pricing tier, optionally with a High Availability option that runs a standby copy in a second Availability Zone.
aws_lightsail_database_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_database_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_database`, which can later be restored into a new database instance.
aws_lightsail_disk: `aws_lightsail_disk` creates a real, SSD-based block storage volume that can be attached to a Lightsail instance for additional or persistent storage beyond the instance's own bundled disk.
aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_disk`, which can later be used to create a new disk with the same data.
aws_lightsail_distribution: `aws_lightsail_distribution` creates a real content delivery network distribution, powered by CloudFront under the hood, that caches and accelerates delivery of content hosted on a Lightsail instance, bucket, or load balancer.
aws_lightsail_domain: `aws_lightsail_domain` creates a real DNS zone within Lightsail for a registered domain, letting its DNS records be managed alongside other Lightsail resources rather than in Route 53 directly.
aws_lightsail_instance: `aws_lightsail_instance` creates a real virtual private server, a bundled combination of compute, storage, and a fixed data transfer allowance, at Lightsail's simplified, predictable monthly pricing.
aws_lightsail_instance_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_instance_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_instance`, including its attached disks, which can later be used to launch a new instance with the same state.
aws_lightsail_load_balancer: `aws_lightsail_load_balancer` creates a real load balancer that distributes incoming traffic across multiple Lightsail instances, Lightsail's own simplified counterpart to an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer.
aws_lightsail_load_balancer_tls_certific: `aws_lightsail_load_balancer_tls_certificate` provisions a real TLS certificate attached to an `aws_lightsail_load_balancer`, so traffic reaching the load balancer over HTTPS terminates against a validated certificate.
aws_lightsail_static_ip: `aws_lightsail_static_ip` allocates a real static public IP address that can be attached to a Lightsail instance, keeping the instance reachable at a fixed address across stops, starts, and replacements.
aws_location_apikey: `aws_location_apikey` creates a real API key for authenticating requests to Amazon Location Service resources, maps, places, routes, trackers, an alternative to IAM credentials introduced for Location Service in January 2024 for simpler client-side and mobile use.
aws_location_geofence_collection: `aws_location_geofence_collection` creates a real collection of virtual geographic boundaries that Amazon Location Service monitors devices against, raising an event when a tracked device enters or leaves one.
aws_location_map: `aws_location_map` creates a real map resource in Amazon Location Service, backed by a chosen map style and data provider, for rendering interactive or static map imagery in an application.
aws_location_place_index: `aws_location_place_index` creates a real place index resource in Amazon Location Service, used to search for and geocode addresses, points of interest, and other place data against a chosen data provider.
aws_location_route_calculator: `aws_location_route_calculator` creates a real route calculator resource in Amazon Location Service, used to estimate travel time and distance and to generate turn-by-turn directions between locations.
aws_location_tracker: `aws_location_tracker` creates a real tracker resource in Amazon Location Service that ingests and stores the near-real-time location of devices, so their movement can be visualized on a map and evaluated against geofences.
aws_location_tracker_consumer: `aws_location_tracker_consumer` links a real `aws_location_tracker` to an `aws_location_geofence_collection` as its consumer, the association that lets a tracker's incoming location updates be evaluated against that collection's geofences.
aws_logs_delivery: `aws_logs_delivery` creates a real, active connection between an `aws_logs_delivery_source` and an `aws_logs_delivery_destination`, the resource that actually turns a configured source and destination into a flowing pipeline of vended logs.
aws_logs_delivery_destination: `aws_logs_delivery_destination` represents a real AWS service, CloudWatch Logs, S3, Firehose, or X-Ray, configured to receive vended logs through the newer CloudWatch Logs delivery framework, the target end of an `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_delivery_source: `aws_logs_delivery_source` represents a real AWS resource, such as a VPC or a Route 53 resolver, registered as a source of vended logs through the newer CloudWatch Logs delivery framework, the origin end of an `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_destination: `aws_logs_destination` creates a real cross-account subscription destination, most commonly a Kinesis stream, that another account's log group subscription filter can stream matching log events to. This is the older CloudWatch Logs subscription mechanism, distinct from the newer delivery-source/delivery-destination framework used by `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_integration: `aws_logs_integration` creates a real, zero-ETL integration between CloudWatch Logs and Amazon OpenSearch Service, currently the only supported integration type, enabling curated vended-log dashboards powered by OpenSearch analytics without a separate ingestion pipeline. Only one integration is currently supported per account, and an existing integration cannot be modified in place.
aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector: `aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector` creates a real machine-learning detector that regularly scans one or more log groups, learns the recurring text patterns in their log fields, and flags anomalies that break from those learned patterns.
aws_logs_log_group: `aws_logs_log_group` creates a real CloudWatch Logs log group, the container that log streams are organized under and that retention, encryption, and access settings are configured against.
aws_logs_metric_filter: `aws_logs_metric_filter` defines a real pattern that CloudWatch Logs evaluates against incoming events in an `aws_logs_log_group`, publishing a CloudWatch metric data point each time a log event matches, the mechanism behind turning free-text logs into alarmable numeric metrics.
aws_logs_query_definition: `aws_logs_query_definition` saves a real, named CloudWatch Logs Insights query for reuse from the console or API, rather than re-typing it for every ad hoc investigation.
aws_logs_scheduled_query: `aws_logs_scheduled_query` runs a real `aws_logs_query_definition`-style Logs Insights query on a recurring schedule and delivers its results automatically to a configured destination, such as an S3 bucket or an EventBridge event bus.
aws_logs_transformer: `aws_logs_transformer` attaches a real ordered pipeline of processors to an `aws_logs_log_group`, applying transformations to each log event at ingestion time so that later Logs Insights queries and metric filters can operate on the transformed, structured version rather than the raw text.
aws_lookout_equipment_inference_schedule: `aws_lookout_equipment_inference_scheduler` schedules real, recurring inference runs against a trained Amazon Lookout for Equipment model, feeding it fresh sensor data on a cadence and surfacing predicted anomalies. Lookout for Equipment closed to new customers on October 7, 2025, and AWS has stated it will be fully discontinued on October 7, 2026, a date roughly six weeks from now; existing customers can keep using it as normal until then, with AWS continuing security, availability, and performance investment but no new features.
aws_lookout_vision_project: `aws_lookout_vision_project` was a real project container for training and hosting Amazon Lookout for Vision computer-vision defect-detection models. Lookout for Vision is now fully discontinued: it closed to new customers on October 10, 2024, and shut down entirely on October 31, 2025, a date now in the past, so this resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_m2_application: `aws_m2_application` defines a real mainframe application, its runtime engine (Micro Focus or Blue Age) and application definition, deployed onto an `aws_m2_environment` under AWS Mainframe Modernization. The Mainframe Modernization managed-runtime-environment experience closed to new customers on November 7, 2025; existing customers can continue using it as normal.
aws_m2_environment: `aws_m2_environment` creates a real managed runtime environment, the compute cluster that AWS Mainframe Modernization continually monitors and self-heals, that one or more `aws_m2_application`s run on. Like `aws_m2_application`, this closed to new customers on November 7, 2025; existing customers can continue using it as normal.
aws_macie_allow_list: `aws_macie_allow_list` defines a real list of text patterns or exact values, stored as an S3 object, that Amazon Macie should ignore when scanning for sensitive data, keeping known-benign content out of Macie's findings.
aws_macie_findings_filter: `aws_macie_findings_filter` defines real custom criteria, severity, finding type, affected resource, that either narrows which Macie findings a query returns or automatically archives findings matching those criteria, so routine noise doesn't have to be triaged by hand.
aws_managed_blockchain_accessor: `aws_managed_blockchain_accessor` creates a real token-based access credential for Amazon Managed Blockchain's Ethereum node JSON-RPC APIs, an alternative to signing every request with SigV4 that instead authenticates with a bearer token.
aws_managed_blockchain_member: `aws_managed_blockchain_member` creates a real member identity within a Hyperledger Fabric network on Amazon Managed Blockchain, the account-level participant that peer nodes, `aws_managed_blockchain_node`, are created under.
aws_managed_blockchain_node: `aws_managed_blockchain_node` creates a real peer node running within an `aws_managed_blockchain_member`'s participation in a Hyperledger Fabric network on Amazon Managed Blockchain, the compute that actually executes chaincode and maintains the ledger.
aws_media_connect_bridge: `aws_media_connect_bridge` creates a real connection point between an on-premises data center and AWS, moving live video content from the cloud to a local facility or from a local facility to the cloud, depending on the chosen bridge type.
aws_media_connect_bridge_source: `aws_media_connect_bridge_source` adds a real content source to an `aws_media_connect_bridge`, the specific inbound feed the bridge accepts and relays.
aws_media_connect_flow: `aws_media_connect_flow` creates a real managed transport between a live video source and one or more outputs, MediaConnect's original, source-to-outputs architecture for ingesting, distributing, and routing live video within and beyond AWS.
aws_media_connect_flow_entitlement: `aws_media_connect_flow_entitlement` grants a real other AWS account permission to create their own flow subscribed to this `aws_media_connect_flow`'s output, the mechanism MediaConnect uses to share a live feed across account boundaries.
aws_media_connect_flow_output: `aws_media_connect_flow_output` defines a real destination address, protocol, and port that an `aws_media_connect_flow` sends its ingested video to; a single flow can have up to 50 outputs.
aws_media_connect_flow_source: `aws_media_connect_flow_source` defines the real inbound video feed, its protocol and originating address, that an `aws_media_connect_flow` ingests from.
aws_media_connect_flow_vpc_interface: `aws_media_connect_flow_vpc_interface` attaches a real elastic network interface inside a VPC to an `aws_media_connect_flow`, letting the flow send or receive video privately within that VPC instead of over the public internet.
aws_media_connect_gateway: `aws_media_connect_gateway` creates a real on-premises software gateway that connects local infrastructure to AWS Elemental MediaConnect, the component an `aws_media_connect_bridge` uses to actually reach a data center.
aws_media_connect_router_input: `aws_media_connect_router_input` creates a real inbound connection point on the MediaConnect Router, a newer, cloud-native routing backbone that lets any registered feed be instantly connected to any registered destination across regions, distinct from MediaConnect's original per-flow architecture.
aws_media_connect_router_network_interfa: `aws_media_connect_router_network_interface` provisions a real public or VPC-scoped network interface that an `aws_media_connect_router_input` or router output uses to actually send or receive traffic, the underlying network plumbing beneath the MediaConnect Router's logical inputs and outputs.
aws_media_connect_router_output: `aws_media_connect_router_output` creates a real outbound destination on the MediaConnect Router that can receive media routed from one or more `aws_media_connect_router_input`s.
aws_media_convert_job_template: `aws_media_convert_job_template` saves a real, reusable set of MediaConvert transcoding job settings, output format, codec, bitrate, and destination queue, so new jobs can be created from the template instead of re-specifying every setting.
aws_media_convert_preset: `aws_media_convert_preset` saves real, reusable encoding settings for a single output within an `aws_media_convert_job_template` or job, letting the same output configuration, resolution, codec, bitrate, be applied across multiple jobs and overridden per job when needed.
aws_media_convert_queue: `aws_media_convert_queue` creates a real queue that MediaConvert transcoding jobs are submitted to and processed from, in ACTIVE or PAUSED state, with jobs of equal priority processed in the order they were submitted.
aws_media_live_channel: `aws_media_live_channel` creates a real live video encoding channel, MediaLive's core resource, that takes one or more `aws_media_live_input`s and encodes them into one or more outputs.
aws_media_live_channel_placement_group: `aws_media_live_channel_placement_group` organizes a real group of `aws_media_live_channel`s within an `aws_media_live_cluster`, so channels running on the same on-premises or Outposts infrastructure can be managed and allocated together.
aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_templat: `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template` defines a real reusable CloudWatch alarm configuration for MediaLive resources, which can be applied consistently across channels rather than hand-configured per channel.

`aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template_group` groups real `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template`s together so the group, rather than each template individually, can be attached to a MediaLive signal map or channel in one step.
aws_media_live_cluster: `aws_media_live_cluster` creates a real MediaLive Anywhere cluster, the on-premises or Outposts infrastructure grouping that `aws_media_live_channel_placement_group`s and their channels run on, letting MediaLive manage encoding workloads outside AWS's own data centers.
aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_templat: `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template` defines a real reusable EventBridge rule for a MediaLive event type, a channel alert, an input change, a signal map alarm, and more, which can be applied consistently across resources rather than hand-configured per resource.
`aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template_group` groups real `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template`s together so the group can be attached to a MediaLive signal map or channel in one step.
aws_media_live_input: `aws_media_live_input` defines a real video source, its type and connection details, that an `aws_media_live_channel` encodes from.
aws_media_live_input_security_group: `aws_media_live_input_security_group` defines a real set of allowed CIDR ranges that an `aws_media_live_input` accepts push-based input from, MediaLive's equivalent of a security group scoped to incoming video traffic.
aws_media_live_multiplex: `aws_media_live_multiplex` creates a real MPEG-TS multiplex, a single transport stream that carries multiple encoded programs bundled together for broadcast delivery, distinct from an `aws_media_live_channel`'s single-program encoding role.
aws_media_live_multiplexprogram: `aws_media_live_multiplexprogram` adds a real encoded program, video, audio, and metadata settings, into an `aws_media_live_multiplex`'s combined transport stream.
aws_media_live_network: `aws_media_live_network` defines a real network configuration, IP pools and routes, that MediaLive Anywhere uses so channels running on an `aws_media_live_cluster` can reach on-premises or Outposts network resources.
aws_media_live_node: `aws_media_live_node` registers a real physical or virtual compute unit into an `aws_media_live_cluster`, the actual hardware or instance that MediaLive Anywhere schedules channel encoding work onto.
aws_media_live_sdi_source: `aws_media_live_sdi_source` defines a real SDI (Serial Digital Interface) video input, hardware-connected rather than network-streamed, for MediaLive Anywhere to encode from an on-premises `aws_media_live_cluster`.
aws_media_live_signal_map: `aws_media_live_signal_map` discovers and visualizes a real media supply chain, MediaLive channels, MediaConnect flows, and related resources, starting from a chosen entry point ARN, and can attach `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template`s and `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template`s across everything it discovers.
aws_media_package_asset: `aws_media_package_asset` ingests a real video-on-demand asset through an `aws_media_package_channel`, the original MediaPackage architecture's VOD counterpart to its live-streaming role.
aws_media_package_channel: `aws_media_package_channel` creates a real entry point that receives a live video stream from an encoder such as MediaLive and prepares it for packaging, the original MediaPackage (v1) channel resource, now superseded for new deployments by `aws_media_package_v2_channel`.
aws_media_package_origin_endpoint: `aws_media_package_origin_endpoint` defines a real packaging configuration, HLS, DASH, CMAF, and more, on an `aws_media_package_channel`, the endpoint players actually request the packaged stream from.
aws_media_package_packaging_configuratio: `aws_media_package_packaging_configuration` defines a real output packaging format, HLS, DASH, CMAF, MSS, for on-demand assets within an `aws_media_package_packaging_group`.
aws_media_package_packaging_group: `aws_media_package_packaging_group` creates a real top-level container for `aws_media_package_packaging_configuration`s, the v1 MediaPackage VOD counterpart to a live channel.
aws_media_package_v2_channel: `aws_media_package_v2_channel` creates a real entry point that receives a live video stream from an encoder such as MediaLive, MediaPackage v2's redesigned channel resource, which supports low-latency HLS and ingesting via the CMAF-ingest protocol in addition to HLS, distinct from the original `aws_media_package_channel`.
aws_media_package_v2_channel_group: `aws_media_package_v2_channel_group` creates a real top-level MediaPackage v2 resource that one or more `aws_media_package_v2_channel`s belong to, providing a single, fixed egress domain shared across every channel in the group regardless of individual channel failures or upgrades.
aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy: `aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_package_v2_channel`, controlling which principals can ingest into or manage that channel.
aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint: `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint` defines a real packaging configuration on an `aws_media_package_v2_channel`, the endpoint players actually request the packaged output stream from.
aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint_pol: `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint`, controlling which principals can retrieve the packaged output from that endpoint.
aws_media_store_container: `aws_media_store_container` was a real storage container for live video origination in AWS Elemental MediaStore. MediaStore is now fully discontinued: AWS ended access to the MediaStore console and MediaStore resources on November 13, 2025, a date now in the past, recommending migration to S3 for simple live-streaming workflows or to MediaPackage for advanced ones. This resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_media_tailor_channel: `aws_media_tailor_channel` creates a real linear, assembled streaming channel under MediaTailor's channel assembly workflow, stitching together video-on-demand and live sources with personalized ad insertion into one continuous stream.
aws_media_tailor_channel_policy: `aws_media_tailor_channel_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_tailor_channel`, controlling which principals can retrieve its assembled output.
aws_media_tailor_function: `aws_media_tailor_function` defines a real custom function, an HTTP-backed endpoint with configurable headers, that MediaTailor can invoke as part of a sequential executor chain to run custom logic during ad decisioning or playback configuration. This resource has only thin official documentation, verified live this session against AWS's own CloudFormation reference and field schema rather than assumed from general knowledge, since it did not turn up a dedicated conceptual guide page the way MediaTailor's older resources do.
aws_media_tailor_live_source: `aws_media_tailor_live_source` registers a real live content feed under an `aws_media_tailor_source_location`, for use in MediaTailor channel assembly alongside video-on-demand sources.
aws_media_tailor_playback_configuration: `aws_media_tailor_playback_configuration` defines a real playback endpoint configuration, ad decision server settings, manifest processing rules, and CDN configuration, that a player requests a personalized, ad-stitched manifest from.
aws_media_tailor_source_location: `aws_media_tailor_source_location` registers a real origin server, an S3 bucket, web server, CDN, or packaging origin such as MediaPackage, that MediaTailor fetches content manifests from to assemble its own sliding manifest window.
aws_media_tailor_vod_source: `aws_media_tailor_vod_source` registers a real video-on-demand asset under an `aws_media_tailor_source_location`, for use in MediaTailor channel assembly alongside live sources.
aws_memory_db_acl: `aws_memory_db_acl` defines a real Access Control List, the set of users and permissions, that one or more `aws_memory_db_cluster`s authenticate and authorize connections against.
aws_memory_db_cluster: `aws_memory_db_cluster` creates a real MemoryDB cluster, a Redis OSS-compatible, durable in-memory database, with multi-AZ replication and a transaction log that makes it safe to use as a primary database rather than only a cache.
aws_memory_db_multi_region_cluster: `aws_memory_db_multi_region_cluster` creates a real active-active MemoryDB deployment spanning multiple AWS Regions, asynchronously replicating writes between member clusters, typically within about a second, so an application can read and write locally in whichever Region is closest to it. This is a genuinely recent capability: MemoryDB Multi-Region reached general availability in March 2026.
aws_memory_db_parameter_group: `aws_memory_db_parameter_group` defines a real set of engine configuration parameters that can be applied to one or more `aws_memory_db_cluster`s instead of hand-tuning each cluster individually.
aws_memory_db_subnet_group: `aws_memory_db_subnet_group` defines a real set of VPC subnets that an `aws_memory_db_cluster` is allowed to place its nodes into.
aws_memory_db_user: `aws_memory_db_user` creates a real authentication identity, its password or IAM authentication method, that is granted permissions through an `aws_memory_db_acl` to connect to a MemoryDB cluster.
aws_mgn_network_migration_definition: `aws_mgn_network_migration_definition` defines a real source network configuration, read from an S3-hosted description of an on-premises or AWS-based network, on-premises or AWS, that AWS's rehosting migration tooling uses to recreate that network's topology in AWS. This resource sits under AWS Application Migration Service, which AWS rebranded to AWS Transform MGN in June 2026; the rebrand changed the service's name and console, not this resource's own behavior.
aws_mpa_approval_team: `aws_mpa_approval_team` creates a real, named group of approvers under AWS Multi-party approval, so that specific sensitive actions elsewhere in AWS require multiple people from this team to approve before they take effect. A team created this way starts in a pending-activation state; if an invited approver declines or the 24-hour response window expires, activation fails and the stack rolls back, deleting the team. Multi-party approval is a comparatively new AWS service, so behavior here is verified live rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_mpa_identity_source: `aws_mpa_identity_source` registers a real source of approver identities, such as an IAM Identity Center instance, that an `aws_mpa_approval_team` draws its members from.
aws_msk_batch_scram_secret: `aws_msk_batch_scram_secret` associates a real batch of Secrets Manager SASL/SCRAM secrets with an `aws_msk_cluster`, enabling username/password authentication for clients connecting to that cluster.
aws_msk_channel: `aws_msk_channel` creates a real, direct delivery pipeline from an MSK Kafka topic into an Apache Iceberg table, configuring the destination catalog, database, table, and partition spec, without a separate Kafka Connect or Firehose hop in between. This is a newer MSK capability for direct-to-Iceberg ingestion, verified live this session against AWS's own field-level schema rather than general knowledge.
aws_msk_cluster: `aws_msk_cluster` creates a real provisioned Amazon MSK cluster, its broker nodes, storage, and networking, the managed Apache Kafka cluster that topics, consumers, and producers actually connect to.
aws_msk_configuration: `aws_msk_configuration` defines a real set of Kafka broker configuration properties that can be applied to one or more `aws_msk_cluster`s instead of hand-tuning each cluster's brokers individually.
aws_msk_replicator: `aws_msk_replicator` creates a real, managed replication pipeline that continuously copies topics and their data between two MSK clusters, provisioned or serverless, in any combination, used to build cross-Region resilient Kafka applications with identical topic names on both sides.
aws_msk_serverless_cluster: `aws_msk_serverless_cluster` creates a real serverless Amazon MSK cluster that scales Kafka capacity automatically with load, reachable privately from up to five VPCs in the same account through AWS PrivateLink without the broker and storage sizing an `aws_msk_cluster` requires.
aws_msk_vpc_connection: `aws_msk_vpc_connection` creates a real private connection from a VPC to an `aws_msk_cluster` using AWS PrivateLink, letting clients in that VPC reach the cluster's brokers without traversing the public internet.
aws_mwaa_environment: `aws_mwaa_environment` creates a real, provisioned Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow environment, its own Airflow web server, scheduler, and workers running continuously, for orchestrating DAGs stored in S3.
aws_mwaaserverless_workflow: `aws_mwaaserverless_workflow` defines a real YAML- or Python-based workflow that Amazon MWAA Serverless executes on demand or on a schedule without any continuously running Airflow environment to manage, distinct from the always-on `aws_mwaa_environment`. MWAA Serverless is a genuinely new deployment option, announced November 17, 2025, so behavior here is verified live rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_nat_gateway: `aws_nat_gateway` creates a real managed NAT gateway in a public subnet, letting instances in a private subnet initiate outbound traffic to the internet or other VPCs without being directly reachable from outside.
aws_neptune_dbcluster: `aws_neptune_dbcluster` creates a real Neptune Database cluster, a managed, serverless-capable graph database engine supporting Gremlin, openCypher, and SPARQL, built for transactional graph workloads like fraud detection and social-network queries, distinct from the memory-optimized analytics engine behind `aws_neptune_graph_graph`.
aws_neptune_dbcluster_parameter_group: `aws_neptune_dbcluster_parameter_group` defines a real set of cluster-level engine parameters that can be applied to an `aws_neptune_dbcluster` instead of hand-tuning the cluster individually.
aws_neptune_dbinstance: `aws_neptune_dbinstance` creates a real database instance, the compute that actually serves queries, within an `aws_neptune_dbcluster`.
aws_neptune_dbparameter_group: `aws_neptune_dbparameter_group` defines a real set of instance-level engine parameters that can be applied to an `aws_neptune_dbinstance` instead of hand-tuning the instance individually.
aws_neptune_dbsubnet_group: `aws_neptune_dbsubnet_group` defines a real set of VPC subnets that an `aws_neptune_dbcluster`'s instances are allowed to be placed into.
aws_neptune_event_subscription: `aws_neptune_event_subscription` subscribes a real SNS topic to receive notifications about events, failovers, backups, configuration changes, occurring on an `aws_neptune_dbcluster` and its instances.
aws_neptune_global_cluster: `aws_neptune_global_cluster` creates a real multi-Region Neptune deployment, coordinating a primary `aws_neptune_dbcluster` and up to five read-only secondary clusters in other Regions with fast replication and disaster-recovery failover.
aws_neptune_graph_graph: `aws_neptune_graph_graph` creates a real Neptune Analytics graph, a memory-optimized engine built for fast, large-scale graph analytics, data-science workloads, and generative-AI use cases like recommendations, rather than the transactional, always-on database role `aws_neptune_dbcluster` serves; data can be loaded into it from a Neptune Database graph or snapshot.
aws_neptune_graph_graph_snapshot: `aws_neptune_graph_graph_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_neptune_graph_graph`, which can later be used to create a new graph with the same data.
aws_network_acl: `aws_network_acl` creates a real, stateless network access control list scoped to a VPC, a numbered set of allow/deny rules evaluated in order per subnet, distinct from a security group's stateful, instance-scoped rules.
aws_network_firewall_firewall: `aws_network_firewall_firewall` creates a real managed, stateful network firewall attached to a VPC's subnets, enforcing the rules defined by an `aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy` against traffic passing through it.
aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy: `aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy` defines the real set of stateless and stateful rule groups, and default actions, that one or more `aws_network_firewall_firewall`s enforce against passing traffic.
aws_network_firewall_logging_configurati: `aws_network_firewall_logging_configuration` configures real log destinations, CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Kinesis Data Firehose, for an `aws_network_firewall_firewall`'s own alert and flow logs.
aws_network_firewall_rule_group: `aws_network_firewall_rule_group` defines a real, reusable, named set of stateless or stateful traffic-inspection rules that can be referenced from one or more `aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy` resources.
aws_network_firewall_tlsinspection_confi: `aws_network_firewall_tlsinspection_configuration` defines real certificate and scope settings that let an `aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy` decrypt, inspect, and re-encrypt TLS traffic rather than only inspecting it in encrypted form.
aws_network_firewall_vpc_endpoint_associ: `aws_network_firewall_vpc_endpoint_association` attaches a real additional subnet-scoped firewall endpoint to an existing `aws_network_firewall_firewall`, letting one firewall protect multiple VPCs or provide multiple endpoints within a single VPC's Availability Zone, a capability AWS Network Firewall added in May 2025.
aws_network_flow_monitor_monitor: `aws_network_flow_monitor_monitor` creates a real Amazon CloudWatch Network Flow Monitor monitor, scoped to local and remote AWS resources by type, EC2 instances, subnets, VPCs, and more, that reports near-real-time network performance metrics, retransmissions and data transferred, for the actual traffic flowing between them. Network Flow Monitor is a comparatively recent CloudWatch capability, launched at re:Invent in December 2024; this entry is verified against AWS's own field-level schema live this session rather than assumed from general knowledge, since it did not turn up a dedicated CloudFormation reference page the way older resources do.
aws_network_interface: `aws_network_interface` creates a real Elastic Network Interface, a virtual network card with its own private IP addresses and security groups, that can be attached to an EC2 instance.
aws_network_interface_attachment: `aws_network_interface_attachment` attaches a real `aws_network_interface` to a specific EC2 instance at a chosen device index, the resource that actually represents the attach action rather than the interface itself.
aws_network_interface_permission: `aws_network_interface_permission` grants a real cross-account permission on an `aws_network_interface`, letting another AWS account attach that interface to an instance it owns.
aws_network_manager_connect_attachment: `aws_network_manager_connect_attachment` creates a real GRE- or no-encapsulation-based Connect attachment on an `aws_network_manager_core_network`, providing the transport that `aws_network_manager_connect_peer`s establish BGP sessions over.
aws_network_manager_connect_peer: `aws_network_manager_connect_peer` establishes a real BGP peering session over an `aws_network_manager_connect_attachment`, exchanging routes between the core network and an external or on-premises device.
aws_network_manager_core_network: `aws_network_manager_core_network` creates a real, centrally managed global network backbone, the core resource behind AWS Cloud WAN, that VPCs, Direct Connect gateways, and Site-to-Site VPNs attach to and route through.
aws_network_manager_device: `aws_network_manager_device` registers a real physical or virtual on-premises networking device, a router or firewall, into an `aws_network_manager_global_network` so Network Manager can represent it in its own topology and route analysis.
aws_network_manager_direct_connect_gatew: `aws_network_manager_direct_connect_gateway_attachment` attaches a real Direct Connect gateway to an `aws_network_manager_core_network`, extending Cloud WAN's routing to on-premises networks reachable over Direct Connect.
aws_network_manager_global_network: `aws_network_manager_global_network` creates a real top-level container that groups an organization's `aws_network_manager_device`s, `aws_network_manager_site`s, and `aws_network_manager_link`s into a single network Network Manager can visualize and monitor.
aws_network_manager_link: `aws_network_manager_link` defines a real network connection, its bandwidth and provider, between two `aws_network_manager_site`s within an `aws_network_manager_global_network`.
aws_network_manager_site: `aws_network_manager_site` represents a real physical location, an office or data center, within an `aws_network_manager_global_network` that `aws_network_manager_device`s are associated with.
aws_network_manager_site_to_site_vpn_att: `aws_network_manager_site_to_site_vpn_attachment` attaches a real Site-to-Site VPN connection to an `aws_network_manager_core_network`, bringing that VPN's routes into Cloud WAN's centrally managed routing.
aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_peer: `aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_peering` peers a real existing EC2 Transit Gateway with an `aws_network_manager_core_network`, letting workloads on a legacy Transit Gateway reach resources across Cloud WAN.
aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_rout: `aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_route_table_attachment` attaches a real transit gateway route table, exposed through an `aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_peering`, to an `aws_network_manager_core_network`'s own routing.
aws_network_manager_vpc_attachment: `aws_network_manager_vpc_attachment` attaches a real VPC to an `aws_network_manager_core_network`, the mechanism that actually brings a VPC's subnets into Cloud WAN's centrally managed routing.
aws_notifications_contacts_email_contact: `aws_notifications_contacts_email_contact` registers a real email address as a contact that AWS User Notifications can deliver notifications to.
aws_notifications_event_rule: `aws_notifications_event_rule` defines a real EventBridge event pattern under an `aws_notifications_notification_configuration`, matching against AWS-service-sourced events so User Notifications generates a notification whenever a matching event occurs.
aws_notifications_notification_configura: `aws_notifications_notification_configuration` creates a real, named notification configuration in AWS User Notifications, the top-level resource that `aws_notifications_event_rule`s attach to and that ties event matching to delivery channels and aggregation settings.
aws_notifications_notification_hub: `aws_notifications_notification_hub` designates a real AWS Region where AWS User Notifications stores, processes, and replicates an account's notification data, an account-level setting rather than a per-notification resource.
aws_oam_link: `aws_oam_link` creates a real cross-account link from a source account into a monitoring account under CloudWatch Observability Access Manager, sharing a filtered set of that source account's logs, metrics, and traces so they can be viewed centrally without switching accounts.
aws_observability_admin_organization_cen: `aws_observability_admin_organization_centralization_rule` defines a real, organization-wide rule that routes telemetry, logs by source and type, from member accounts to a chosen central destination account, with granular control over which data centralizes versus stays local.
aws_observability_admin_organization_tel: `aws_observability_admin_organization_telemetry_rule` applies a real `aws_observability_admin_telemetry_rule`-style telemetry configuration across every account in an AWS Organization at once, rather than one account at a time.
aws_observability_admin_s3_table_integra: `aws_observability_admin_s3_table_integration` configures a real integration that routes an account's or organization's telemetry data into S3 Tables under CloudWatch Observability Admin, for long-term, queryable storage outside CloudWatch itself.
aws_observability_admin_telemetry_pipeli: `aws_observability_admin_telemetry_pipelines` defines a real telemetry pipeline under CloudWatch Observability Admin, describing how collected telemetry data is processed and routed on its way to a destination.
aws_observability_admin_telemetry_rule: `aws_observability_admin_telemetry_rule` defines a real rule specifying which AWS resources, by type and selection criteria, should have telemetry collection enabled and how, giving CloudWatch Observability Admin a way to audit and enforce telemetry configuration across an account.
aws_odb_cloud_exadata_infrastructure: `aws_odb_cloud_exadata_infrastructure` provisions a real Oracle Exadata infrastructure, physical Exadata compute and storage, within Oracle Database@AWS, the underlying hardware layer that `aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster`s are created on top of. Oracle Database@AWS runs on infrastructure managed by Oracle Cloud Infrastructure but delivered from within AWS's own data centers.
aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster: `aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster` creates a real Exadata VM cluster on top of an `aws_odb_cloud_exadata_infrastructure`, the compute layer that Oracle databases actually run on within Oracle Database@AWS, requiring both an Exadata infrastructure and an `aws_odb_network` to already exist.
aws_odb_network: `aws_odb_network` creates a real network, peered to an Amazon VPC, that lets EC2 application servers reach Oracle Exadata databases running under Oracle Database@AWS; provisioning an `aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster` requires an ODB network to already exist.
aws_omics_annotation_store: `aws_omics_annotation_store` creates a real store for genomic annotation data, such as variant effect predictions, that AWS HealthOmics workflows can read from and write to.
aws_omics_configuration: `aws_omics_configuration` sets real account-level default run configuration for AWS HealthOmics workflow runs, such as default VPC subnet and security group settings, so individual `aws_omics_workflow` runs don't need to specify that configuration every time.
aws_omics_reference_store: `aws_omics_reference_store` creates a real store for reference genome sequences that `aws_omics_sequence_store` data and `aws_omics_workflow` runs are aligned against.
aws_omics_run_cache: `aws_omics_run_cache` configures a real cache location for an `aws_omics_workflow`'s task outputs, letting a later run reuse a previous run's completed task results instead of recomputing them.
aws_omics_run_group: `aws_omics_run_group` defines a real named limit, on compute or duration, that one or more AWS HealthOmics workflow runs are grouped under and constrained by.
aws_omics_sequence_store: `aws_omics_sequence_store` creates a real store, backed by S3, for raw genomic sequence files, such as FASTQ, BAM, or CRAM, that AWS HealthOmics workflows read from.
aws_omics_variant_store: `aws_omics_variant_store` creates a real store for variant call data, such as VCF or gVCF output, that AWS HealthOmics workflows can query and analyze.
aws_omics_workflow: `aws_omics_workflow` defines a real bioinformatics workflow, its WDL, Nextflow, or CWL definition and parameters, that AWS HealthOmics runs against genomic data in an `aws_omics_sequence_store` or `aws_omics_reference_store`.
aws_omics_workflow_version: `aws_omics_workflow_version` publishes a real, immutable version of an `aws_omics_workflow`'s definition, letting runs pin to a specific version rather than always using the workflow's current definition.
aws_open_search_serverless_collection: `aws_open_search_serverless_collection` creates a real OpenSearch Serverless collection, a set of indexes for search, time-series, or vector-search workloads that scales its own OpenSearch Compute Units automatically without cluster management.
aws_open_search_serverless_collection_gr: `aws_open_search_serverless_collection_group` creates a real group of `aws_open_search_serverless_collection`s that share OpenSearch Compute Units at the group level, even across collections encrypted with different KMS keys, reducing cost versus provisioning capacity per collection. Collection groups are a recent addition to OpenSearch Serverless's next-generation architecture, introduced in February 2026.
aws_open_search_serverless_index: `aws_open_search_serverless_index` defines a real index, its mappings and settings, within an `aws_open_search_serverless_collection`.
aws_open_search_service_application: `aws_open_search_service_application` creates a real OpenSearch Service Application, a unified analytics workspace that spans multiple `aws_open_search_service_domain`s and OpenSearch Serverless collections behind one access point, distinct from a domain's own role as a single managed cluster.
aws_open_search_service_domain: `aws_open_search_service_domain` creates a real, managed OpenSearch cluster, its data nodes, dedicated master nodes, and storage, OpenSearch Service's original, cluster-provisioned resource, distinct from the auto-scaling `aws_open_search_serverless_collection`.
aws_organizations_account: `aws_organizations_account` creates a real new member AWS account inside an AWS Organization, provisioned and joined to the organization directly rather than invited separately.
aws_organizations_organizational_unit: `aws_organizations_organizational_unit` creates a real container within an AWS Organization's hierarchy that groups `aws_organizations_account`s and other OUs, so `aws_organizations_policy` resources like service control policies can be attached once and apply to everything nested under it.
aws_organizations_policy: `aws_organizations_policy` creates a real policy, a service control policy, tag policy, backup policy, AI services opt-out policy, or declarative policy, that can be attached to an AWS Organization, an `aws_organizations_organizational_unit`, or an `aws_organizations_account` to govern what that target and everything under it can do.
aws_organizations_resource_policy: `aws_organizations_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based policy at the AWS Organizations management account level, a narrower, newer counterpart to the identity- and OU-targeted `aws_organizations_policy`, controlling which principals can call Organizations APIs against the organization itself.
aws_osis_pipeline: `aws_osis_pipeline` creates a real, fully managed OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline, a serverless Data Prepper configuration (in YAML) that filters, transforms, and routes data from a source such as S3 into an OpenSearch domain or collection without infrastructure to manage.
aws_outposts_site: `aws_outposts_site` registers a real physical location, its address and operating hours, where an AWS Outposts rack or server will be installed, extending AWS infrastructure and APIs into that on-premises facility.
aws_panorama_application_instance: `aws_panorama_application_instance` deployed a real computer-vision application onto an AWS Panorama appliance. AWS Panorama is now fully discontinued: it closed to new customers on May 20, 2025, and AWS ended support entirely on May 31, 2026, a date now in the past, after which the console, its resources, and the Panorama Appliances customers purchased all stopped functioning. This resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_panorama_package: `aws_panorama_package` defined a real container of the model, code, and assets that ran as an `aws_panorama_application_instance` on an AWS Panorama appliance. Like the rest of AWS Panorama, this is fully discontinued: closed to new customers May 20, 2025, with AWS ending support entirely on May 31, 2026, a date now in the past.
aws_panorama_package_version: `aws_panorama_package_version` published a real, immutable version of an `aws_panorama_package`. This resource describes the now fully discontinued AWS Panorama service, which ended support on May 31, 2026.
aws_payment_cryptography_alias: `aws_payment_cryptography_alias` creates a real friendly name for an `aws_payment_cryptography_key`, so application code can reference the alias rather than a key ARN and keep working unchanged when the underlying key is rotated. A key can have multiple aliases, but each alias points to exactly one key at a time.
aws_payment_cryptography_key: `aws_payment_cryptography_key` creates a real cryptographic key purpose-built for payment processing use cases, PIN translation, card data encryption, key exchange, hosted in a managed, PCI-compliant environment distinct from general-purpose `aws_kms_key`s.
aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector: `aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector` creates a real connector between an `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority` and an Active Directory domain, letting AWS Private CA act as a drop-in replacement for a self-managed enterprise CA and issue certificates to domain-joined objects through AD's own auto-enrollment and group policy features, without deploying or patching local agents.
aws_pcaconnector_ad_directory_registrati: `aws_pcaconnector_ad_directory_registration` registers a real Active Directory with AWS Private CA Connector for AD, the prerequisite step an `aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector` for that directory depends on.
aws_pcaconnector_ad_service_principal_na: `aws_pcaconnector_ad_service_principal_name` registers a real Kerberos service principal name in Active Directory on behalf of an `aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector`, letting the connector authenticate to the domain the way a domain-joined service would.
aws_pcaconnector_ad_template: `aws_pcaconnector_ad_template` defines a real certificate template, mirroring an AD certificate template's own settings, that an `aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector` issues certificates against.
aws_pcaconnector_ad_template_group_acces: `aws_pcaconnector_ad_template_group_access_control_entry` grants a real AD security group permission to enroll for certificates against an `aws_pcaconnector_ad_template`, controlling who can actually request a certificate from that template.
aws_pcaconnector_scep_challenge: `aws_pcaconnector_scep_challenge` creates a real, static SCEP password that a device or mobile device management system presents to an `aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector` to authenticate its certificate enrollment request.
aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector: `aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector` creates a real connector that lets mobile devices and networking gear enroll for certificates from an `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority` using the Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol, the mechanism a mobile device management solution typically calls.
aws_pcs_cluster: `aws_pcs_cluster` creates a real AWS Parallel Computing Service cluster, a managed Slurm scheduler with its controller and accounting database, that `aws_pcs_compute_node_group`s and `aws_pcs_queue`s attach to for running HPC workloads without self-managing the scheduler.
aws_pcs_compute_node_group: `aws_pcs_compute_node_group` defines a real group of compute nodes, statically scaled login nodes or elastically scaled worker nodes, attached to an `aws_pcs_cluster`, the resource that actually runs submitted HPC jobs.
aws_pcs_queue: `aws_pcs_queue` defines a real Slurm job queue on an `aws_pcs_cluster`, associated with one or more `aws_pcs_compute_node_group`s that jobs submitted to it are scheduled onto.
aws_personalize_dataset: `aws_personalize_dataset` imports real interaction, item, or user data, conforming to an `aws_personalize_schema`, into an `aws_personalize_dataset_group` for Amazon Personalize to train recommendation models against.
aws_personalize_dataset_group: `aws_personalize_dataset_group` creates a real top-level container that groups the `aws_personalize_dataset`s Amazon Personalize trains an `aws_personalize_solution` from.
aws_personalize_event_tracker: `aws_personalize_event_tracker` creates a real endpoint that streams live user interaction events, clicks, purchases, views, into an `aws_personalize_dataset_group`, so an already-deployed campaign can incorporate real-time behavior rather than only the data it was originally trained on.
aws_personalize_metric_attribution: `aws_personalize_metric_attribution` configures real, ongoing export of business metrics, click-through rate, conversion, tied back to an `aws_personalize_solution`'s recommendations, so their real-world impact can be measured outside Personalize itself.
aws_personalize_schema: `aws_personalize_schema` defines a real Avro schema describing the structure of interaction, item, or user data, that one or more `aws_personalize_dataset`s must conform to when imported.
aws_personalize_solution: `aws_personalize_solution` trains a real recommendation model against the data in an `aws_personalize_dataset_group`, using either a built-in Personalize recipe or AutoML, the resource that actually produces the model a deployed campaign serves recommendations from.
aws_pinpoint_admchannel: `aws_pinpoint_admchannel` enables a real push-notification channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app` for devices reachable through Amazon Device Messaging (Amazon's own Fire OS push service). Amazon Pinpoint's engagement surface, including its channel resources, is being retired: AWS closed Pinpoint to new customers on May 20, 2025, and the Pinpoint console and its resources become inaccessible after October 30, 2026, a date roughly two months from now. The underlying push-delivery capability itself continues under AWS End User Messaging.
aws_pinpoint_apnschannel: `aws_pinpoint_apnschannel` enables a real push-notification channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app` for iOS devices through Apple Push Notification service. Like the rest of Pinpoint's engagement surface, this becomes inaccessible after October 30, 2026 (upcoming, roughly two months out), though APNs push delivery itself continues under AWS End User Messaging.
aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel: `aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel` enables a real APNs sandbox (development/testing) push channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app`, the narrower, non-production counterpart to `aws_pinpoint_apnschannel`, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel: `aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel` enables a real VoIP push-notification channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app` through Apple's APNs VoIP service, used to wake a calling app for an incoming call rather than to show a standard notification, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement as `aws_pinpoint_apnschannel`.
aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel: `aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel` enables the real sandbox (development/testing) counterpart to `aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel`, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_app: `aws_pinpoint_app` creates a real Pinpoint project, the top-level container that channels, segments, campaigns, and templates are organized under. AWS closed Amazon Pinpoint to new customers on May 20, 2025, and the Pinpoint console and its engagement resources, endpoints, segments, campaigns, journeys, templates, and analytics, become inaccessible after October 30, 2026, a date roughly two months from now. AWS's guidance is to move engagement workloads toward Amazon Connect and other services; SMS, push, voice, and OTP delivery continue under the rebranded AWS End User Messaging, and email delivery continues under Amazon SES.
aws_pinpoint_application_settings: `aws_pinpoint_application_settings` configures real account-level defaults, quiet hours, campaign hook, limits, for an `aws_pinpoint_app`, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement as the rest of its engagement surface.
aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel: `aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel` enables a real push-notification channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app` for Android devices in China reachable through Baidu Cloud Push, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement as Pinpoint's other channel resources.
aws_pinpoint_campaign: `aws_pinpoint_campaign` creates a real, scheduled or triggered messaging campaign targeting an `aws_pinpoint_app` segment. Campaigns are explicitly named among the engagement features AWS is retiring: the Pinpoint console and campaign resources become inaccessible after October 30, 2026, a date roughly two months from now, with AWS recommending Amazon Connect for continued engagement use cases.
aws_pinpoint_email_channel: `aws_pinpoint_email_channel` enables a real email-sending channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app`, backed by Amazon SES. Like Pinpoint's other channels, this becomes inaccessible after October 30, 2026 (roughly two months from now), but ongoing email sending capability continues directly under Amazon SES, which AWS recommends as the migration target for Pinpoint email workloads.
aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set: `aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set` defines a real set of rules, event destinations, dedicated IP pool, reputation options, applied to emails sent through an `aws_pinpoint_app`'s `aws_pinpoint_email_channel`, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement, with equivalent configuration-set functionality continuing directly under Amazon SES.
aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set_eve: `aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set_event_destination` routes real email sending events, opens, bounces, complaints, from an `aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set` to a destination such as CloudWatch or Kinesis Data Firehose, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_email_dedicated_ip_pool: `aws_pinpoint_email_dedicated_ip_pool` groups real dedicated sending IP addresses under an `aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set`, so a chosen subset of an account's dedicated IPs is used for a particular category of email, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_email_identity: `aws_pinpoint_email_identity` verifies a real sending domain or email address for use with an `aws_pinpoint_email_channel`, the SES-backed identity-verification step required before Pinpoint (or SES directly) will send mail from it.
aws_pinpoint_email_template: `aws_pinpoint_email_template` creates a real, reusable email template, subject line, HTML and text bodies, that an `aws_pinpoint_campaign` or direct send call can reference instead of specifying content inline, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_event_stream: `aws_pinpoint_event_stream` streams a real `aws_pinpoint_app`'s app and campaign events to a Kinesis stream or Firehose delivery stream, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement as the rest of its analytics surface.
aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel: `aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel` enables a real push-notification channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app` for Android devices through Firebase Cloud Messaging (the successor branding of Google Cloud Messaging), subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_in_app_template: `aws_pinpoint_in_app_template` creates a real, reusable in-app message template, layout and content shown inside an application's own UI rather than as a push notification, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_push_template: `aws_pinpoint_push_template` creates a real, reusable push-notification template shared across an `aws_pinpoint_app`'s push channels, ADM, APNs, Baidu, GCM, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_segment: `aws_pinpoint_segment` defines a real, filtered subset of an `aws_pinpoint_app`'s endpoints, by attribute, behavior, or location, that an `aws_pinpoint_campaign` targets. Segments are explicitly named among the engagement features retiring when the Pinpoint console and resources become inaccessible after October 30, 2026, roughly two months from now.
aws_pinpoint_sms_template: `aws_pinpoint_sms_template` creates a real, reusable SMS message template that an `aws_pinpoint_campaign` or direct send call can reference, subject to the same October 30, 2026 Pinpoint retirement.
aws_pinpoint_smschannel: `aws_pinpoint_smschannel` enables a real SMS-sending channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app`. Like Pinpoint's other channels, this becomes inaccessible after October 30, 2026 (roughly two months from now), but SMS delivery capability itself continues under the rebranded AWS End User Messaging.
aws_pinpoint_voice_channel: `aws_pinpoint_voice_channel` enables a real voice-messaging channel on an `aws_pinpoint_app`, delivering automated voice calls. Like Pinpoint's other channels, this becomes inaccessible after October 30, 2026 (roughly two months from now), but voice delivery capability itself continues under the rebranded AWS End User Messaging.
aws_pipes_pipe: `aws_pipes_pipe` creates a real EventBridge Pipes point-to-point integration, pulling events from a single source, SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, MSK, self-managed Kafka, or Amazon MQ, optionally filtering, enriching, and transforming them, and delivering the result to a single target, without hand-writing the glue code an equivalent Lambda function would need.
aws_placement_group: `aws_placement_group` creates a real EC2 placement group, a placement strategy, cluster for low-latency networking within an Availability Zone, spread for maximum hardware isolation, or partition for large distributed workloads, that instances are then launched into.
aws_proton_environment_account_connectio: `aws_proton_environment_account_connection` establishes a real cross-account IAM role that lets an AWS Proton management account provision an `aws_proton_environment_template`'s resources into a separate target account, without the target account's own credentials being shared. AWS Proton is being discontinued: it closed to new customers on October 7, 2025, and AWS will end support on October 7, 2026, a date roughly a month and a half from now.
aws_proton_environment_template: `aws_proton_environment_template` defines a real, reusable infrastructure template, the shared networking, cluster, or platform resources that one or more services deploy onto, in AWS Proton's own template-driven provisioning model. AWS Proton is being discontinued: closed to new customers October 7, 2025, with support ending October 7, 2026, a date roughly a month and a half from now; deployed infrastructure keeps running after that date even though the Proton console and API stop being accessible.
aws_proton_service_template: `aws_proton_service_template` defines a real, reusable service template, the application-level resources deployed on top of an `aws_proton_environment_template`'s shared infrastructure. Like the rest of AWS Proton, this is being discontinued, with support ending October 7, 2026, roughly a month and a half from now.
aws_qbusiness_application: `aws_qbusiness_application` creates a real Amazon Q Business application, the top-level container for an enterprise's own indexed data, retrievers, plugins, and web experience in this generative-AI assistant service. Amazon Q Business closed to new customers on July 31, 2026, a date roughly three weeks in the past from now; existing customers keep full support, security patches, and bug fixes, but no new features, and AWS is steering new use cases toward Amazon Quick, the evolution of what was Amazon QuickSight.
aws_qbusiness_data_accessor: `aws_qbusiness_data_accessor` grants a real external ISV application cross-account access to query an `aws_qbusiness_application`'s index through the SearchRelevantContent API, so that ISV's own product can surface an organization's Q Business content without duplicating it. This inherits Q Business's own closed-to-new-customers status as of July 31, 2026.
aws_qbusiness_data_source: `aws_qbusiness_data_source` configures a real connector, SharePoint, S3, a web crawler, and many more, that feeds content into an `aws_qbusiness_index`.
aws_qbusiness_index: `aws_qbusiness_index` creates a real search index within an `aws_qbusiness_application` that one or more `aws_qbusiness_data_source`s populate and that an `aws_qbusiness_retriever` reads from to ground the application's generative answers.
aws_qbusiness_permission: `aws_qbusiness_permission` grants a real resource-based permission on an `aws_qbusiness_application`'s index to a specific external account, the mechanism underlying an `aws_qbusiness_data_accessor`'s cross-account read access.
aws_qbusiness_plugin: `aws_qbusiness_plugin` connects a real third-party or custom action, such as creating a ticket or updating a record in another system, to an `aws_qbusiness_application`, letting its assistant take actions rather than only answer questions.
aws_qbusiness_retriever: `aws_qbusiness_retriever` adds a real retrieval configuration to an `aws_qbusiness_application`, pointing it at either its own native `aws_qbusiness_index` or an existing Amazon Kendra index as the source of grounding content for its generated answers.
aws_qbusiness_web_experience: `aws_qbusiness_web_experience` creates a real, hosted chat front end for an `aws_qbusiness_application`, so end users can interact with it directly in a browser rather than only through the API.
aws_qldb_ledger: `aws_qldb_ledger` created a real, cryptographically verifiable, append-only ledger database. Amazon QLDB is now fully discontinued: AWS ended support on July 31, 2025, a date well over a year in the past, with little formal notice, recommending migration to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL's ledger-style extensions, which do not preserve QLDB's own cryptographic verifiability. This resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_qldb_stream: `aws_qldb_stream` streamed a real, continuous feed of an `aws_qldb_ledger`'s journal changes to a Kinesis Data Stream. Like the ledger itself, this describes the now fully discontinued Amazon QLDB service, which ended support July 31, 2025.
aws_quick_sight_action_connector: `aws_quick_sight_action_connector` connects a real external system, a SaaS application or internal API, to Amazon Quick (the AI-workspace product that Amazon QuickSight was renamed into, first as Amazon Quick Suite on October 9, 2025 and shortened to Amazon Quick in 2026), letting its agents take real write actions in that system rather than only read data from it. The underlying CloudFormation namespace remains `AWS::QuickSight::*` despite the product rename.
aws_quick_sight_approval_policy: `aws_quick_sight_approval_policy` defines a real rule governing when an `aws_quick_sight_action_connector`'s write actions require human approval before they execute versus running automatically, part of Amazon Quick's own agentic-action governance.
aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions: `aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions` defines a real, named set of restricted capabilities, disabling the ability to share dashboards, for example, that can be assigned to specific QuickSight/Amazon Quick users or groups, layered on top of standard Author or Reader permissions.
aws_quick_sight_data_set: `aws_quick_sight_data_set` defines a real, queryable dataset, built from one or more `aws_quick_sight_data_source`s with its own joins, calculated fields, and row-level security, that dashboards and analyses in QuickSight/Amazon Quick are built against.
aws_quick_sight_data_source: `aws_quick_sight_data_source` defines a real connection to an external system, a database, S3, or a SaaS application, that one or more `aws_quick_sight_data_set`s pull data from.
aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting: `aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting` configures real data loss prevention enforcement for Amazon Quick, applying Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to control (block, warn, or allow) how files are handled across Quick's spaces, chat, and knowledge bases. This is a genuinely new integration, announced in August 2026, so behavior here is verified live rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_quick_sight_flow: `aws_quick_sight_flow` defines a real Quick Flow, an automated, multi-step workflow within Amazon Quick, part of the AI-workspace capabilities QuickSight evolved into after its October 2025 rename to Amazon Quick Suite (shortened to Amazon Quick in 2026).
aws_quick_sight_folder: `aws_quick_sight_folder` creates a real folder that organizes `aws_quick_sight_data_set`s, dashboards, analyses, and other QuickSight/Amazon Quick assets, and that permissions can be applied to in bulk rather than per asset.
aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base: `aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base` connects a real content source, SharePoint, OneDrive, and similar, into Amazon Quick's Quick Index component, so its agents can ground answers in that organization's own documents.
aws_quick_sight_oauth_client_application: `aws_quick_sight_oauth_client_application` registers a real OAuth client that an `aws_quick_sight_action_connector` uses to authenticate to the external system it connects to.
aws_quick_sight_refresh_schedule: `aws_quick_sight_refresh_schedule` schedules real, recurring refreshes of an `aws_quick_sight_data_set`'s underlying data, on a daily, weekly, monthly, or custom cadence.
aws_quick_sight_space: `aws_quick_sight_space` creates a real Quick Space, a collaborative workspace within Amazon Quick where files, chat, and knowledge bases are shared among a defined group of users, part of the AI-workspace capabilities QuickSight evolved into.
aws_quick_sight_theme: `aws_quick_sight_theme` defines a real, reusable set of colors, fonts, and layout options that can be applied to dashboards in QuickSight/Amazon Quick, so visual styling stays consistent without configuring it dashboard by dashboard.
aws_quick_sight_topic: `aws_quick_sight_topic` defines a real natural-language topic, an `aws_quick_sight_data_set` plus curated field synonyms and calculations, that QuickSight/Amazon Quick's Q&A feature answers plain-English questions against.
aws_quick_sight_topic_v2: `aws_quick_sight_topic_v2` defines a newer-generation version of an `aws_quick_sight_topic`, Amazon Quick's current natural-language topic configuration, superseding the original topic resource's schema for new topics.
aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection: `aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection` creates a real, persistent elastic network interface into a VPC that an `aws_quick_sight_data_source` can route through to reach a database that isn't publicly reachable.
aws_ram_permission: `aws_ram_permission` defines a real, reusable managed permission, the specific set of actions a principal is allowed on a shared resource, that an `aws_ram_resource_share` attaches instead of relying only on the resource's own default permission.
aws_ram_resource_share: `aws_ram_resource_share` creates a real cross-account resource share, listing the specific resource ARNs, principal accounts or organizational units, and permissions involved, the core AWS Resource Access Manager resource that actually grants another account access to a resource without duplicating it.
aws_rbin_rule: `aws_rbin_rule` creates a real Recycle Bin retention rule that intercepts deletion of a matching resource, an EBS snapshot or EBS-backed AMI, retaining it in the bin for a configured period so it can be recovered instead of being permanently deleted immediately.
aws_rds_cluster_snapshot: `aws_rds_cluster_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_rds_dbcluster`, which can later be restored into a new cluster.
aws_rds_custom_dbengine_version: `aws_rds_custom_dbengine_version` registers a real custom database engine version, a customer-provided installation image, for use with RDS Custom, letting an `aws_rds_dbinstance` run a specific, customer-controlled engine build rather than only AWS's own standard RDS engine versions.
aws_rds_dbcluster: `aws_rds_dbcluster` creates a real Aurora (or Multi-AZ) database cluster, the storage and coordination layer that one or more `aws_rds_dbinstance`s attach to for compute.
aws_rds_dbcluster_parameter_group: `aws_rds_dbcluster_parameter_group` defines a real set of cluster-level engine parameters that can be applied to an `aws_rds_dbcluster` instead of hand-tuning the cluster individually.
